metadata.name: goldeneye-metal
metadata.description: GoldenEye Metal is an experimental, source-only static recompilation project focused on a native Apple Silicon and Metal rendering path. This repository contains the runtime, toolchain, Metal backend, and game integration in one tree.

releases.name: GoldenEye Metal v0.5.1
releases.body:
Reliability update for GoldenEye Metal.

- Improved Metal rendering and shader-cache reliability
- Safer save and profile writes
- Audio callback and shutdown stability fixes
- Expanded campaign and multiplayer regression testing

Signed and notarized for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer.

Game data is not included.

releases.name: GoldenEye Metal v0.5.0
releases.body:
Major native Metal, stability and diagnostics update.

- Improved Metal rendering, synchronization and frame pacing
- Stronger controller, pause and local multiplayer handling
- Optional one-frame GPU capture for easier diagnostics
- Expanded crash, fault-injection and sanitizer coverage
- New gameplay, multiplayer and release validation automation
- Experimental exact Xenos EDRAM work included for continued development

Signed and notarized for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer.
 This remains an experimental release.

releases.name: GoldenEye Metal v0.4.2
releases.body:
Gameplay stability update.

- Prevents a critical-section ownership deadlock that could freeze gameplay
- Prevents failed sound creation from crashing 3D audio location updates
- Adds focused regression checks and diagnostic markers for both issues

Signed and notarized for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer.

readme_text:
# GoldenEye Metal

Play GoldenEye 007 on your Mac, with native Apple Silicon code and Metal rendering. Use keyboard
and mouse or a modern controller, switch between original and remastered graphics, and play local
split-screen with up to four players.

**[Download v0.5.1 for macOS (.dmg)](https://github.com/ysrdevs/goldeneye-metal/releases/download/v0.5.1/GoldenEye-Metal-0.5.1-macos-arm64.dmg)** ·
[Release notes](https://github.com/ysrdevs/goldeneye-metal/releases/tag/v0.5.1) ·
[Watch gameplay](https://youtu.be/VkbwbXw2tPw) ·
[Discord](https://discord.gg/2AKEFgR7)

[![GoldenEye Metal gameplay on macOS](https://img.youtube.com/vi/VkbwbXw2tPw/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/VkbwbXw2tPw)

GoldenEye Metal is playable today. Development continues on performance, rendering accuracy and
compatibility across more Macs and missions.

## Play on macOS

You need:

- an Apple Silicon Mac;
- macOS 14 or newer; and
- a compatible game backup that you are legally authorized to use.

To start playing:

1. [Download the DMG](https://github.com/ysrdevs/goldeneye-metal/releases/download/v0.5.1/GoldenEye-Metal-0.5.1-macos-arm64.dmg).
2. Open it and drag **GoldenEye Metal.app** into Applications.
3. Launch the app. On first use, select your compatible local game backup and wait for the
   one-time import.
4. Choose **Play GoldenEye**. Future launches open the same launcher with your private local copy
   ready.

The first-run launcher accepts:

- the compatible original game-backup ZIP;
- the Xbox LIVE/STFS package stored inside that backup; or
- an extracted folder containing `default.xex`, `files/`, `music.xwb`, and `sfx.xwb`.

The launcher verifies the supported game revision before importing it. Your files stay on your
Mac: the app does not include, download, or upload game data. You can choose a different source
from the launcher later.

If a game session does not close cleanly, the launcher offers **Start in Safe Mode** for one run or
**Play Normally**. You can also choose **Export Diagnostic Bundle…** and send the resulting ZIP
with a report; by default it excludes game data, saves, cache, settings, and GPU captures. If you
explicitly select **Include GPU capture**, the ZIP includes one frame trace that may contain game
memory, so share it only when you intend to.

Choose **Manage Saves…** to create a portable `.gesave` backup, restore a backup, or reset local
progress. Restore and reset preserve the previous data so the action can be undone immediately.

The release is Developer ID signed, Apple-notarized, and stapled. See the
[player guide](docs/PLAYER_GUIDE.md) for detailed controls, controller setup, import behavior, and
troubleshooting.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard and mouse |
| --- | --- |
| Move | WASD |
| Look | Mouse |
| Fire | Left click |
| Aim | Right click |
| A / confirm | Space |
| B / back | Shift |
| Start | Return |
| D-pad | Arrow keys |
| Original / remastered graphics | F |
| Host settings / release cursor | Escape |
| Quit | Command-Q |

Modern controllers work over USB or Bluetooth, including DualShock 4, DualSense, Xbox One, and
Xbox Series X|S controllers. Controllers can be connected or removed while the game is running,
and keyboard/mouse can remain active at the same time. The Controls page includes Modern,
Classic, and Southpaw layouts plus per-button remapping.

## What this project is

GoldenEye Metal is not a traditional full-system emulator. The game code is recompiled ahead of
time for ARM64, while a compatibility runtime provides the Xbox 360 APIs and GPU behavior the game
expects.

The graphics path consumes the game's real command stream and shaders, translates the shaders,
and renders the result directly through Metal:

```text
game commands -> Xenos shader translation -> Metal rendering -> game resolve -> presentation
```

There is no Vulkan or MoltenVK graphics path in the macOS release. The repository contains the
runtime, recompilation toolchain, Metal backend, native launcher, and game integration source.

## Features

Working today:

- single-player campaign gameplay and two- to four-player local split-screen;
- original and remastered graphics switching during play;
- native keyboard/mouse input, stable P1–P4 gamepad ports, presets, and remapping;
- a local game-data importer, crash-aware Safe Mode, save management, true local-mission pause,
  and diagnostic export;
- live performance presets, MetalFX/Sharp output scaling, filtering, FXAA and colour controls;
- optional FPS or detailed performance overlays and a diagnostics-ready 60-second report;
- a guarded Testing page with 14 runtime cheats and Unlock Next Level / Unlock All Levels;
- clean macOS window/menu quitting.

Metal renders the game internally at its native **1280x720**. Bilinear, Sharp, and MetalFX Spatial
can scale that image to the window or Retina display, but they do not increase the game's internal
rendering resolution.

The latest recorded development-build tests averaged **59.85 FPS** across two Dam runs on an
**M3 Ultra**. Performance varies by Mac, settings and scene; this is not a locked-60-FPS promise.
Broader campaign, multiplayer and hardware testing continues alongside rendering improvements.

For implementation details, evidence, milestones, known gaps, and the exact next priorities, read
the [native Metal technical status](docs/GOLDENEYE_NATIVE_METAL_PROJECT_STATUS.md).

| Platform | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Apple Silicon macOS | Playable — native ARM64 + Metal, campaign gameplay and local split-screen |
| Windows and Linux | Backend code exists, but this project's current changes are not verified there |

## Build and contribute

Source builds require an Apple Silicon Mac, current Xcode Command Line Tools, CMake, Git, and a
compatible local `default.xex` that you are authorized to use. Game data and generated game code
are intentionally excluded from Git.

- [Development guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) — configure, build, code generation, tests, manual runs,
  input diagnostics, and Metal profiling
- [macOS distribution](docs/MACOS_DISTRIBUTION.md) — app packaging, Developer ID signing,
  notarization, ZIP, and DMG creation
- [Contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) — development expectations and pull requests
- [Technical status](docs/GOLDENEYE_NATIVE_METAL_PROJECT_STATUS.md) — architecture, proof,
  milestones, blockers, and roadmap

Developers with a completed local source build can also double-click
[Launch GoldenEye.command](<Launch GoldenEye.command>) to run the build-tree version with Metal and
native input selected automatically.

## Game data, licensing, and trademarks

This repository does not include the original XEX, generated recompiled C++, audio banks,
captures, or extracted game assets. Do not commit or request downloads for those files. Each user
is responsible for supplying compatible files they are legally authorized to use.

This is a multi-license source tree. See [LICENSE](LICENSE),
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), and the license files inside vendored and
submodule directories.

This project is unofficial and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any game publisher, console
manufacturer, or trademark owner. Product names are used only to identify compatibility targets.
No trademark or game-content rights are granted by this repository.

metadata.name: black-macos-recomp
metadata.description: Black (Xbox, 2006) static recompilation to native macOS Apple Silicon. Project code only; bring your own disc. See METHODOLOGY.md.

readme_text:
# black-recomp

Static recompilation port of **Black** (Xbox, 2006) to macOS on Apple Silicon.

The game's x86 code is translated function-by-function to C and compiled
natively for arm64. The Xbox kernel, GPU (NV2A) and audio (MCPX APU) are
replaced by the runtime in the `xboxrecomp` toolkit, which is a required
sibling checkout. Nothing here emulates a CPU.

**No game code or assets are in this repository.** You must supply your own
legally obtained copy of the disc. Nothing of the game's is committed, in this
tree or in its history; `.gitignore` keeps `game_files/`, `*.xbe`, `*.iso`,
`*.xiso`, the build directory and the evidence screenshots out.

## Status

Boots to the title screen, plays the intro videos, reaches the first mission
and is playable: move, aim, shoot, reload, objectives. Rendering goes through
the NV2A renderer of xemu extracted from QEMU. The boot is still unstable
during video playback (about one run in three), camera drift after firing is
unresolved, and audio is silent because the APU's DSP56300 GP/EP is a stub.

The port's running notes live in the toolkit repository, in
`black-port-progreso-ajustado.md` and `BLACK_PORT_ESTADO_2026-09-19.md`.

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/main_posix.c` | Host: boot, XBE load, window, framebuffer present, crash handler |
| `src/recomp_natives.c` | Guest functions written by hand instead of translated |
| `src/recomp_manual.c` | Function-name lookup for the `[MENU]` log, ICALL and UNIMPL diagnostics |
| `src/shadow.c` | Optional differential check against the original x86 (`-DBLACK_SHADOW=ON`) |
| `seeds/hand_seeds.json` | Functions only reachable through pointers, which the analysis cannot find |
| `tools/shadow_wrap.py` | Generator wrapper for the shadow build |
| `play.sh` | Run it |
| `evidence.sh` | Screenshot and pad-state recording |

`src/recomp/gen/` is **generated** and not committed. Regenerate it from the
toolkit; see `REGENERATE.md`. Without it the project will not build.

## Quick start

```sh
mkdir black && cd black
git clone https://github.com/elpetese/black-macos-recomp.git
git clone https://github.com/elpetese/black-macos-runtime.git xboxrecomp
git -C xboxrecomp submodule update --init --recursive
pip3 install capstone unicorn
cd black-macos-recomp && ./reproduce.sh /path/to/your/Black.iso
BLACK_GAME_DIR=$PWD/game_files ./play.sh
```

`reproduce.sh` extracts your disc, lifts the game to C and builds it. It uses
`analysis/black-analysis.tar.xz`, a function database (addresses and call
graph only; no game code or assets). Details: [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md).

## Build

Needs a sibling `../xboxrecomp` checkout, plus SDL3, glib, epoxy and
libxxhash via pkg-config. On macOS, CMake and clang from Xcode are enough.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/elpetese/black-macos-recomp.git
git clone https://github.com/elpetese/black-macos-runtime.git xboxrecomp   # the toolkit
git -C xboxrecomp submodule update --init --recursive

cd black-macos-recomp
cmake -S . -B build-mac -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build-mac --target black-recomp -j8
```

Full step-by-step reproduction (extract your disc, lift, build, debug): see [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md).

`CMakeLists.txt` looks for the toolkit at `../xboxrecomp`; point
`-DXBOXRECOMP_DIR=` elsewhere if you keep it somewhere else.

### Metal renderer (ANGLE)

A second build runs xemu's renderer on OpenGL ES through ANGLE's Metal
backend: about 30 fps in level 1 at the default scale, against about 15 for
the OpenGL build. You build ANGLE yourself (it is not in this repo); the
step-by-step is in [METHODOLOGY.md, section 9](METHODOLOGY.md#9-faster-renderer-build-angle-metal-backend).

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-angle -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DXEMU_ANGLE_LIB_DIR=/path/to/angle/out/Release
cmake --build build-angle --target black-recomp -j8
./play.sh                 # ANGLE is the default; ANGLE=0 uses build-mac
```

## Run

```sh
./play.sh                 # full screen, Metal (ANGLE) build, short videos, 1920x1440
FAST=0 ./play.sh          # full videos (first level in ~7 min instead of ~1.5)
WINDOWED=1 ./play.sh       # start in a window
SCALE=2 ./play.sh         # 1280x960 if the level load ever freezes
ASPECT=4:3 ./play.sh      # the game renders widescreen; 4:3 adds side bars
FOV=70 ./play.sh          # the original uses 70 (default here is 90)
ANGLE=0 ./play.sh         # desktop OpenGL build (build-mac) instead of ANGLE
```

`play.sh` needs the game directory. It defaults to `./game_files`; see `METHODOLOGY.md` for the full reproduction steps. Override with
`BLACK_GAME_DIR=<folder containing default.xbe>`. The log of the run goes to
`build-angle/last-run.log` (`build-mac/` with `ANGLE=0`).

## Controls

The game window needs focus.

| Key | Xbox pad | In Black |
|---|---|---|
| W A S D | Left stick | Move |
| Mouse (or I J K L) | Right stick | Look / aim |
| Left click | Right trigger | Fire |
| Right click | Left trigger | Aim down sights (zoom) |
| E (or Space) | A | Use, pick up, open doors; accept in menus |
| C or Ctrl | B | Crouch |
| R | X | Reload |
| Wheel, 1 / 2 (or Q) | Y | Change weapon |
| G or side mouse button | White | Throw grenade |
| F or V | Black | Melee |
| B or X | Left-stick click | Fire mode |
| Shift | Right-stick click | Precision aim |
| Arrows, 3 / 4 | D-pad | Menus, quick select |
| Esc (or Enter) | Start | Pause (Esc also frees the mouse) |
| Tab | Back | Mission objectives |
| Cmd+Return | | Toggle full screen |

To play: Enter on the title, Space or E on START MISSION, NORMAL, the mission
briefing, then wait for "RENDEZVOUS WITH BLACK CELL" (about 40 s after the
level loads; the game ignores the pad before that).

## Environment variables

Set by `play.sh`; useful on their own for diagnosing a hang.

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `RECOMP_VBLANK=1` | **Required.** Without it the title waits for the NV2A interrupt forever |
| `RECOMP_AC97_READY=1` | AC'97 codec, DSP ACK thread, D3D pushbuffer fence. Without it the boot dies at `sub_00084F90` after 19 file opens instead of 52 |
| `RECOMP_XEMU_GPU=1` | The xemu NV2A renderer |
| `RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1` | Pushbuffer executor |
| `RECOMP_FB_WINDOW=1` | Framebuffer window |
| `RECOMP_USB=1` | Emulated OHCI, for the title's own USB stack |
| `RECOMP_AUDIO_TEST=1` | 440 Hz test tone through the APU |
| `RECOMP_AUDIOLOG=1` | Audio flow every 2 s: buffers, drops, underruns |
| `RECOMP_AUDIO_DUMP=<f>` | Every submitted buffer to a file, s16 stereo 48 kHz |
| `RECOMP_HANG_DUMP=<s>` | If no frame is presented for s seconds, dump every thread |
| `RECOMP_MENULOG=1` | Name the menu actions the front end dispatches |
| `RECOMP_XINLOG=1` | One line whenever the pad state the game reads changes |
| `RECOMP_DRAWDUMP=1` | Per-flip draw dumps (touch `/tmp/black_dump` for the next frame) |
| `RECOMP_FB_SNAP=<dir>/` | One screenshot per second |
| `RECOMP_KEEP_BLACK_PANEL=1` | Draw the opaque black panel the menus ask for; off by default, the filter that hides it is in `main_posix.c` |
| `RECOMP_FOV=<deg>` | Field of view |
| `RECOMP_XEMU_DRAWLOG=L<n>` | Draw log for the n-th frame with more than 300 draws |

## Known issues

- **Boot instability during videos** (high). About one run in three crashes or
  hangs before the menu: a crash in `sub_0013DD20` reaching `0x9xxxxxxx` when an
  XMV video ends, a main-loop crash with the stack overwritten, or a hang at
  ~37 s. Run with `RECOMP_HANG_DUMP`; several of the FPU-precision,
  per-thread dispatch and IRQL fixes made later may already reduce it.
- **Camera drifts to the floor** (high), after firing. Ruled out: the pad
  reports correct axes. The weapon-recoil recovery is overshooting.
- **Video quality** (medium). Heavy blocking; may be another SSE/MMX case in the
  recompiler.
- **Black panel and collapsed menu text** (medium). The filter in `main_posix.c`
  hides the panel, but the title's own menu logic is what asks for it, and it
  also collapses some text to a point. The pause menu is invisible because of it.
- **PS4 controller** (medium). SDL sees 0 joysticks; needs the SDL input
  subsystem and Input Monitoring permission on macOS.
- **Audio** (unresolved). The pipeline reaches SDL2 but the APU's DSP56300
  GP/EP is a stub. The sibling runtime now mixes even numbered APU bins left
  and odd numbered bins right, so Black's observed bins 20 and 19 reach
  separate channels. Its ADPCM decoder also accepts the reserved header byte
  and clamps the initial step index. These changes improve basic playback;
  DSP effects and a faithful final mix still need the real GP/EP. The
  `RECOMP_REAL_DSP=1` implementation is present but not wired into the build
  or APU dispatch yet. Run with `RECOMP_AUDIO_TEST=1` to verify host output;
  that tone bypasses the game's voice and DSP pipeline.

## Credits

- [sp00nznet/xboxrecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp) — the
  toolkit this is built on, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 sp00nz
- [xemu](https://github.com/xemu-project/xemu) — the MCPX APU and NV2A
  renderer, LGPL-2.1, Copyright (c) 2012 espes, 2018-2019 Jannik Vogel,
  2019-2025 Matt Borgerson
- [mborgerson/dsp56300](https://github.com/mborgerson/dsp56300) — DSP56300
  interpreter and JIT, MIT
- Ubisoft / Southend Interactive — *Black*. Not affiliated; no assets here.

releases.name: V0.1.6
releases.body:
# Conker's Bad Fur Day: Recompiled V0.1.6

Almost everything in it started as a report, a request or a test from someone playing. Thank you all, credits are at the bottom. 🐿️

## New

- **Save states.** F5 saves the game exactly as it is, anywhere. F7 loads it back, and F6 picks one of nine slots. States made by an earlier version usually still load, and they never touch the game's own save. More in [`docs/save-states.md`](https://github.com/sciaschi/CBFD-Recompiled/blob/master/docs/save-states.md). (#94)
- **Achievements.** 37 of the program's own, from your first death to the end of the game, plus one for reaching every scene. They're in the new **Achievements** settings tab and kept on your computer, with no account needed. Only what you do while playing counts. A save that's already further along unlocks them again as a new game reaches each scene, and loading a save state earns nothing.
- **Reticle.** A green aiming ring like Live & Reloaded's. (#74)
- **Overscan Borders.** Hides the N64's black border down each side of the picture, without stretching it. (#72)
- **Swap Sticks plays like a shooter.** A real strafe, the shotgun's laser on R, and Lock-On can be turned off. (#84)
- **Conker's Detail.** Keeps Conker on his most detailed model, so he no longer swaps models as he moves.
- **The Russian fan translation plays.** Load it with **Add ROM**, and it shows as **Version: US Russian**.
- **Settings reorganised.** The tabs scroll, Camera and Mouse & Gyro have their own tabs, and Texture Pack has moved to Graphics.

## Fixed

**Crashes**
- Returning to the starting area after the horror chapter no longer crashes, and Windy no longer stops when the game runs out of memory. Busy scenes were overrunning the frame's drawing lists. (#98)
- The smoke over Windy's beehive no longer crashes the game.
- Connecting a controller while playing no longer crashes on macOS. (#88)
- Mods no longer stop the game on macOS. (#81)

**Camera and aiming**
- Free camera: looking up raises the view once the camera is low, and it stays steady at walls and the floor. (#70)
- In the bank's slow-motion leaps, the mouse moves the crosshair. (#85)

**Graphics**
- Windy's tickly bees no longer vanish beside the old 4:3 area in widescreen, and the sunflower is no longer drawn over bees in front of it. (#101)
- Split screen: every player's view draws its own level, not just the last player's. In widescreen, every view is widened the same way, with characters and HUD centred. (#78)
- Shadows: no dark patch for a frame when walking into a room, no dark line following Conker, and no growing between frames. (#73, #75, #76)
- Conker no longer snaps between poses while moving. (#76)
- Drunk Conker's blurry vision is back. (#77)
- Steam Deck: the left 4:3 bar shows correctly. (#82)
- Light glows, like the lamps over the Feral Reserve's doors, stay visible past the old 4:3 edges.

**Other**
- RetroAchievements is removed, since it doesn't accept recompilations. The program's own achievements take its place.

## Known issues

- **Rock Solid with modded-audio ROMs:** the sliding rock cutscene can get stuck on some ROM hacks. A fix is ready and waiting on a test. (#79)
- **Cutscene dialogue is sometimes missing.** It's intermittent and hard to reproduce, so if it happens to you, please say where in #99.

## Thank you

Every one of these came from someone taking the time to report, describe, record or test:

- **[@IceBaronTwinAcc](https://github.com/IceBaronTwinAcc)** played through the whole game and reported as they went:
  - the crash after the horror chapter (#98);
  - the culled tickly bees (#101);
  - the bank's slow-motion aiming (#85).
  They also tested each fix on Linux, and reported the missing dialogue (#99).
- **[@urbangangsta101](https://github.com/urbangangsta101)** asked for save states (#94) and tried every test build on Linux and the Steam Deck until they were solid. They also suggested the Swap Sticks improvements (#84) and rounded up a list of V0.1.5 bugs (#82).
- **[@KohlsAdrian](https://github.com/KohlsAdrian)** tracked down two macOS crashes: mods (#81) and connecting a controller mid-game (#88). They also started the Hollywood Subtitles mod, which is coming along in #108.
- **[@huguitocloud](https://github.com/huguitocloud)** helped narrow down the macOS mod crash (#81) and the V0.1.5 bugs (#82). They also found the exact ROM bytes behind the Rock Solid softlock (#79).
- **[@jxlanda](https://github.com/jxlanda)** reported the black line following Conker (#73) and the dark flickering shadow (#75), and helped with the free camera (#70).
- **[@drencoss](https://github.com/drencoss)** reported the free camera's problems (#70).
- **[@fizzlepicklepop](https://github.com/fizzlepicklepop)** asked for the reticle (#74) and the overscan option (#72).
- **[@Urshak84](https://github.com/Urshak84)** and **[@Rukario](https://github.com/Rukario)** reported and helped pin down Conker's stuttery animation (#76).
- **[@Atrus99](https://github.com/Atrus99)** noticed the drunk vision was gone (#77).
- **[@fufiplayyy](https://github.com/fufiplayyy)**, **[@blackpath92-code](https://github.com/blackpath92-code)** and **[@dankor66](https://github.com/dankor66)** reported and tested split screen (#78).
- **[@Shurrick](https://github.com/Shurrick)** asked for the Russian translation.
- **[@nitrostemp](https://github.com/nitrostemp)** for the macOS port.
- **[DevOldSchool](https://github.com/DevOldSchool/conkers-bfd-decomp)** for the decomp, which keeps making the game easier to understand.

If something's still not right, please open an issue: that's how most of this list came about. Thanks again, everyone.

releases.name: V0.1.5
releases.body:
## Conker's Bad Fur Day: Recompiled V0.1.5

### New
- **Right Stick: Free Camera** (General tab, off by default). In single player the right stick turns the camera around Conker and tilts it up and down, the same way the mouse camera does. While it's turning the camera it no longer presses C-buttons. R-Look, aiming and cutscenes still use the right stick as the C-buttons. Thanks @drencoss (#39) and @TheIntruder666 (#65).
- **Camera: Field of View**, set in degrees (50° is the original). The sky and the game's view follow it, and the level now draws everything the wider view can see. Thanks @drencoss (#39) and @TheIntruder666 (#65).
- **Camera: Invert Turning** gains **Invert Y** and **Invert Both**, for tilting the free camera.
- **Mouse: Turn the Camera** (On/Off): use the mouse for aiming only and keep the game's camera. With it on, the stick and the mouse now turn the camera together, where before the mouse stopped the stick. Thanks @leansteak096-blip (#60).
- **Show FPS** (Graphics tab, off by default) shows two numbers in the top-right corner:
  - **FPS** is the frames shown on screen, including interpolated ones. If it drops, your PC is falling behind.
  - **Game** is the frames the game itself makes, up to 30. If only this one drops, it's the game's own slowdown.
- **Texture packs** (#63):
  - RT64 packs (`.rtz`, or a folder with an `rt64.json`) load from the new **Settings > Texture Packs** tab.
  - GLideN64 HD packs (`.htc`) can be installed from the **Mods** menu, or put in the `mods` folder. Each is converted once, with its progress shown, and then works like an RT64 pack.
  - `tools/texture_packs/gliden64_to_rt64.py` converts a GLideN64 pack to a `.rtz` ahead of time.
  - Thanks @MrVenom-32 for the request and for testing every build until `.htc` packs installed, and @EliParker28.
- **Cutscene Aspect Ratio** (Graphics tab, default Expand). Set to 4:3, it draws black bars over everything outside the 4:3 picture during every cutscene, so you don't see characters waiting beside the frame for their cue. The game itself stays widescreen. Thanks @Atrus99 (#21), who tracked down the scenes the first versions missed.
- **Rumble settings:** each controller now gets its own player's rumble, so in multiplayer player 1's rumble no longer shakes every controller. You can choose which motor rumbles (small, large or both), the style (smooth or on/off) and the strength. Thanks @Rukario (#62) for reporting it and confirming the fix.
- **Mouse buttons can be bound** to controls, shown with mouse button icons. Thanks @SteelRain36 (#61).
- **N64 controllers and adapters** (#28):
  - Built-in mappings cover raphnet-tech adapters, Mayflash, Hyperkin, the Nintendo Switch Online N64 controller and the 8BitDo 64.
  - Pads that SDL maps as Switch controllers now get their C-buttons on the right stick, as the game's controls expect.
  - Each connected controller is written to the log with its ID, to help with controller reports.
  - Thanks @dCo3lh0 for the detailed reports and logs, and @lopenator.

### Fixes
- **Mouse and gyro aiming** now work in the sniper scope, with the magnum and throwables, and with the dual SMGs, where the aim no longer springs back to the middle. Both scale with the zoom. The aiming settings are now grouped into Camera, Stick, Mouse and Gyro, and your saved sensitivities carry over. Thanks @SteelRain36 (#61).
- **Music:** the right song now plays every time. Thanks @TemporaryCrown (#66) for the reports, and @Atrus99 for testing the fix.
  - The new song now starts after a game over and reloading a save.
  - The stone dragon's mouth no longer switches to the level's music at full volume and keeps it going until a game over.
  - The outside ambience no longer carries on inside the bar.
  - Songs no longer play over each other.
- **Lighting:** Conker's point lights light what they should again. The wall and lantern outside the bar, the inside of the bar and the N64 logo are no longer dark or dim. Thanks @Atrus99 (#21) for testing.
- **Reflections:** reflective surfaces such as the glass Conker holds and the Rare medallion's sheen now show their reflection. Thanks @Atrus99 (#21) for testing.
- **Cutscenes:** camera cuts no longer flash, or show the camera passing through the scenery between two shots. Thanks @DRok17 (#59) for reporting it with a video, and @Atrus99 for testing.
- **Cutscenes in widescreen:** speech bubbles are no longer cut off at the 4:3 edge. Thanks @DRok17 and @Atrus99 (#59).
- **Crash in fullscreen at 4K on Direct3D 12:** the old 4:3 cutscene setting switched the renderer's aspect ratio for every cutscene, which crashed there. The black bars avoid it. Thanks @Atrus99 (#21) for the crash logs and the many test runs.
- **Widescreen:** the thin blue line at the right edge of the screens before the N64 logo is gone.
- **AMD integrated graphics** (e.g. Ryzen laptops and mini PCs) now start in Vulkan when the graphics API is set to Auto, instead of crashing at launch in Direct3D 12. Thanks @FellOutThree (#64) for reporting it and confirming the fix.

### For contributors
- **CONTRIBUTING.md** explains how changes get in, where patches live, naming, documentation and testing.
- **Issue forms** for bug reports and feature requests ask for the version, system, GPU, graphics API, settings and `crash.log`.
- **Licenses:** the release now includes the GPL 3 text, and README, CONTRIBUTING and `LICENSES.txt` explain what the licenses mean for builds. The texture pack hashing code is GPL 2 or later.

### Known issues
- **Direct3D 12:** if the game crashes for you, switch to Vulkan. Set the graphics API in Settings > Graphics, or set `api_option` to `"Vulkan"` in `graphics.json` in the data folder.
- **Cutscene Aspect Ratio at 4:3** also puts bars over the B pads' hints. The game marks no difference between those and story scenes.
- **raphnet-tech adapters** have built-in mappings but haven't been tested on real hardware yet (#28).
- **Glows at the screen edges:** in widescreen, light glows still disappear toward the left and right edges.
- **Linux (some KDE setups):** the ROM file dialog may not appear. As a workaround, run it once as `./ConkerRecomp --rom /path/to/rom.z64`. The ROM is kept for later runs (#30).
- **macOS:** requires macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later (#24).

Thank you to everyone who reported issues, sent logs and videos, and tested builds for this release: @Atrus99, @TemporaryCrown, @dCo3lh0, @lopenator, @drencoss, @TheIntruder666, @leansteak096-blip, @DRok17, @SteelRain36, @Rukario, @MrVenom-32, @EliParker28 and @FellOutThree.

releases.body:
## Conker's Bad Fur Day: Recompiled V0.1.4

### New
- **Mouse camera.** Set Mouse Sensitivity above 0 and the mouse orbits the camera around Conker, with the scroll wheel zooming in and out (within the controller's camera distances). The camera stops and slides along walls the way the game's own camera does. C-Left/C-Right, cutscenes, special cameras and aiming (hold R) hand the camera back to the game.
- **Mouse and gyro aiming in R-Look** (hold R to look around), with separate invert and response settings (Smooth or Direct) for the stick, mouse and gyro. Thanks @christopher-conley (#35).
- **R-Look: Invert Stick now also covers the second aiming mode**: the sniper scope, the magnum and throwables. Thanks @CtrlP1 (#47).
- **Camera: Invert Turning and Camera: Turning Speed** (50–300%) for turning the camera with C-Left/C-Right or the right stick in single player. Multiplayer strafing isn't affected. Thanks @CtrlP1 (#47).
- **Skip Intro mod**: boots straight to the bar, a button press from the main menu. Thanks @christopher-conley (#36).
- **The included mods now come with each release**, in a separate Mods zip (Skip Intro, Skip Any Cutscene, Cheats). Copy the `.nrm` files into the game's mods folder, or add them from the launcher's Mods menu (#14).

### Fixes
- **Multiplayer:** one Start press no longer joins players 2–4 at once. Each controller now gets its own player slot, in the order the controllers first press a button, and the keyboard stays with player 1. Thanks @CtrlP1 (#37).
- **Split-screen multiplayer in widescreen:** both players' views are now widened, not just the bottom one.
- **Widescreen:** doors and objects near the sides of the screen no longer lose pieces or vanish depending on the camera angle (e.g. the Feral Reserve doors, the Windy caves' "CLOSED" door). Also fixed at 21:9 and 32:9.
- **Widescreen:** the drunk effect at the start of the game no longer smears into streaks (#51).
- **Ultrawide:** bubbles, bees and sparkles are now drawn all the way to the edges on very wide screens (32:9).
- **Light glows** no longer fade out with distance, e.g. the lights on the Feral Reserve sign.
- **Empty areas of the screen** (such as where the camera is inside a wall) now show black instead of a smeared copy of the last frame.

### Known issues
- **Glows at the screen edges:** in widescreen, light glows still disappear toward the left and right edges.
- **Controller rumble** is shared in multiplayer: player 1's rumble shakes every controller.
- **Linux (some KDE setups):** the ROM file dialog may not appear. As a workaround, run it once as `./ConkerRecomp --rom /path/to/rom.z64`; the ROM is kept for later runs (#30).
- **macOS:** requires macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later (#24).

readme_text: # Conker's Bad Fur Day: Recompiled A native PC port of **Conker's Bad Fur Day** (N64, US version). It's built by statically recompiling the game with [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp), starting from the [Conker decompilation](https://github.com/mkst/conker). It runs on [N64ModernRuntime](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64ModernRuntime) and is rendered by [RT64](https://github.com/rt64/rt64). > **This repository contains no game data.** You need your own legally obtained > copy of the US ROM. Everything from the game is extracted from that ROM on > your machine during the build. ## Download Ready-to-play Windows, Linux and macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later) builds are on the [Releases page](https://github.com/sciaschi/CBFD-Recompiled/releases). Unpack one anywhere, run `ConkerRecomp`, and pick your US ROM in the launcher the first time. The packages contain no game data: you still need your own ROM. The macOS app isn't signed with an Apple developer ID, so the first time, open it and then choose **Open Anyway** in System Settings > Privacy & Security. To build it yourself instead, read on. ## Features - Runs natively on Windows (Direct3D 12 or Vulkan), Linux (Vulkan) and macOS (Metal), rendered by RT64. Supports higher resolutions, widescreen, anti-aliasing and high frame-rate presentation, with Conker, his shadow and the camera interpolated between the game's frames. - Widescreen across gameplay, menus, cutscenes (or 4:3 cutscenes, with the **Cutscene Aspect Ratio** option), split screen and the pause screen, with the world drawn and culled for the wider view. **Overscan Borders** hides the N64's black border down each side. - Game controllers and keyboard, with remappable controls (mouse buttons too) and rumble settings (motor, style and strength). N64 pads and adapters for real N64 controllers are built in, and each controller gets its own player in multiplayer. - Mouse and gyro aiming, a free camera on the right stick (or the mouse) that stays out of walls, camera turning speed and inversion, and a Field of View setting. - An aiming **Reticle**, a green ring like Live & Reloaded's, and **Swap Sticks** and **Lock-On** options for aiming. - Full audio: music, sound effects and the voice acting. - Saving (EEPROM), stored per user. - A launcher with settings, controls and a mod menu (RecompFrontend, as in Zelda 64: Recompiled and Banjo: Recompiled). - The game's reflective surfaces (Conker's glass, the logo's sheen) and its point lights (the bar's lantern, the N64 logo), drawn as on the N64. - **Conker's Detail** keeps Conker on his most detailed model, and **Show FPS** puts a frame rate counter in the corner. - Achievements, the program's own, for reaching the game's scenes. - ROM hacks that only change the game's assets, such as the uncensored and the Russian translation ROMs, with the launcher switching between them. - Mod support (`.nrm` mods: function patches and hooks). Three mods are included: **Skip Intro**, **Skip Any Cutscene** and **Cheats**. - Texture packs (RT64's `.rtz`, and GLideN64's `.htc`), for HD textures and other replacements. - Save states: save anywhere with F5 and load with F7, in nine slots ([how to use them, and how they work](docs/save-states.md)). ## Status The game is playable, and has been played through to the end. Known issues: - Widescreen: the pause menu's blurred background is the 4:3 frame scaled up to the full width, so its top and bottom are cropped. - Only the US ROM is supported (and ROM hacks that only change its assets: see [ROM hacks](#rom-hacks)). - Linux: the game is played on Linux with real GPU drivers, the Steam Deck included, and the build is tested on Ubuntu 24.04. Reports from other distributions and GPUs are welcome, especially about performance or audio. - macOS: the game is played on Apple Silicon with Metal (the build is tested on an Apple M3 Pro with macOS 27 and Xcode 27). It hasn't been confirmed played through on macOS yet, and Intel Macs haven't been tried. If the game crashes on Windows, a report is written to `crash.log` next to the executable and shown in a message box. On Linux and macOS, the crash report is printed to the terminal. Please include it when reporting a problem. ## What you need to build it - The **US** ROM of Conker's Bad Fur Day in big-endian `.z64` format, with SHA-1 `4cbadd3c4e0729dec46af64ad018050eada4f47a`. It is never committed: the build extracts what it needs from your copy. - A folder path without an apostrophe (`'`) to clone into. Some of RT64's build steps break on one. Then follow the guide for your system: [Windows](#building-on-windows), [Linux](#building-on-linux) or [macOS](#building-on-macos). Each is one command once the tools are installed. The first full build takes a while, because the recompiled game is a lot of C code. ## Building on Windows Windows 10 or 11 (x64). Everything builds natively; `build.cmd` does all of it. ### 1. Install the tools (once) - [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win). - [Python 3](https://www.python.org/downloads/). In the installer, tick *Add python.exe to PATH*. - **Visual Studio 2022 or later** with the *Desktop development with C++* workload. The free *Build Tools for Visual Studio* edition is enough. ### 2. Get the code and build In a Command Prompt, in the folder you want it in (for example `D:\Games`), with the path to your ROM: ```bat git clone --recursive https://github.com/sciaschi/CBFD-Recompiled.git cd CBFD-Recompiled build.cmd "C:\path\to\your\conker.z64" ``` The first build takes a while. When it's done, the game is `host\build-win\ConkerRecomp.exe` (see [Playing](#playing)). ### Updating ```bat git pull build.cmd ``` The script updates the submodules and their patches, and only rebuilds what changed. ## Building on Linux Tested on Ubuntu 24.04 (x86-64). You need a Vulkan driver: Mesa's, which most distributions install by default, or NVIDIA's. ```sh git clone --recursive https://github.com/sciaschi/CBFD-Recompiled.git cd CBFD-Recompiled ./build.sh ~/path/to/your/conker.z64 ``` On Ubuntu and Debian, the script lists the packages it's missing and offers to install them. On other distributions, install the equivalents of `git python3 cmake ninja-build clang pkg-config libsdl2-dev libdbus-1-dev libfreetype-dev` yourself. When it's done, run `host/build/ConkerRecomp` (see [Playing](#playing)). To update: `git pull`, then `./build.sh` again. ## Building on macOS macOS on Apple Silicon or Intel. The game renders with Metal. `build.sh` does all of it, as on Linux. ### 1. Install the tools (once) - **Xcode**, from the App Store. The Command Line Tools alone aren't enough: RT64 compiles its shaders with Xcode's Metal compiler. Open Xcode once to finish its setup. If `xcode-select -p` doesn't print a path inside `Xcode.app`, run `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app`. - [**Homebrew**](https://brew.sh). - Optionally, for building mods: `brew install llvm` (Apple's clang can't compile for the N64's MIPS processor). ### 2. Get the code and build In Terminal, in the folder you want it in, with the path to your ROM: ```sh git clone --recursive https://github.com/sciaschi/CBFD-Recompiled.git cd CBFD-Recompiled ./build.sh ~/path/to/your/conker.z64 ``` Put the ROM's path in quotes if it has spaces or an apostrophe, for example `./build.sh "$HOME/Downloads/Conker's Bad Fur Day (USA).z64"`. The first build takes a while. If some tools are missing, the script lists the Homebrew packages (`cmake ninja pkg-config sdl2 freetype`) and offers to install them. It also offers to download Xcode's Metal Toolchain (about 850 MB), which Xcode 26 and later install separately. When it's done, the game is `host/build/ConkerRecomp` (see [Playing](#playing)). To turn it into a standalone `ConkerRecomp.app` that runs without Homebrew (as the release workflow does), run `sh host/package_macos.sh` after `brew install dylibbundler`. The app ends up in `host/build/`. ### Updating ```sh git pull ./build.sh ``` The script updates the submodules and their patches, and only rebuilds what changed. ## What the build does `build.sh` holds the full sequence, if you'd rather run the steps yourself: 1. Checks your ROM (copied to `conker/baserom.us.z64`) and applies the patches in `recomp/` to N64Recomp, N64ModernRuntime and RT64. 2. Builds N64Recomp. 3. Runs `recomp/recompile.py`, which unpacks the game's code from your ROM and recompiles it into `RecompiledFuncs/`. Which functions there are, and where, comes from `recomp/conker.us.syms.toml`: names, addresses and sizes, but no code. The code itself only ever comes from your ROM. 4. Builds the game (`host/`) with CMake. ### Working on the decompilation `recomp/conker.us.syms.toml` (and `mods/syms/`) are generated from the decompilation in `conker/`, which needs its own Linux tools: IDO, which runs through the MIPS binutils, and the Python packages in `requirements.txt`. On Linux, macOS, or in WSL on Windows, `./build.sh --decomp` builds the decompilation too, checks that it rebuilds your ROM's code byte for byte, and regenerates those files from it (`recomp/run.sh`). The decompilation is a work in progress, and most of the code is still the original assembly. [DevOldSchool's conkers-bfd-decomp](https://github.com/DevOldSchool/conkers-bfd-decomp) is further along, and this project follows its progress ([issue #57](https://github.com/sciaschi/CBFD-Recompiled/issues/57)). On macOS, `--decomp` also needs `coreutils` and `mips-linux-gnu-binutils` from Homebrew (the script offers to install them). The decompilation comes with two Linux programs, the IDO compiler and a patched gzip that compresses exactly as the original game's did, so the script puts macOS replacements in `tools/macos/`: IDO's macOS build from [ido-static-recomp](https://github.com/decompals/ido-static-recomp), and GNU gzip 1.10 built with the same one-line change. ## Playing Run `host/build/ConkerRecomp` (Linux and macOS) or `host\build-win\ConkerRecomp.exe` (Windows). The first time, pick **Load ROM** in the launcher and select your ROM (the same `baserom.us.z64` works). After that it's remembered, so just choose **Start Game**. - **Settings** (in the launcher, or Esc / the controller's menu button in game) has its options by tab: General (deadzone, rumble), Camera (turning, the free camera, field of view, aiming with the stick), Mouse & Gyro, Graphics (resolution, aspect ratio, anti-aliasing, frame rate, texture packs), Controls, Sound, Achievements and Mods. The tabs scroll sideways when they don't all fit. - **Achievements** are the program's own, for reaching the game's scenes (the ones its Chapters menu lists), from the first death to the end credits. They're kept on this computer, in `achievements.txt` with the settings, and the Achievements tab lists them. Only what you do in play counts: scenes a save had already reached unlock when a new game reaches them. - Saves, settings and the stored ROM live in `~/.config/ConkerRecompiled` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/ConkerRecompiled` on macOS and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ConkerRecompiled` on Windows. Put an empty `portable.txt` next to the executable to keep them there instead. - **Save states**: F5 saves the game exactly as it is, F7 loads it back, F6 picks the next of the nine slots. They never touch the game's own saves. See [docs/save-states.md](docs/save-states.md). - Default keyboard controls: move with WASD, A = Space, B = Left Shift, Z = Q, L = E, R = R, Start = Enter, C buttons = arrow keys, D-pad = IJKL. Everything can be remapped in Controls. - N64 pads and adapters for real N64 controllers (raphnet-tech's, Mayflash, Hyperkin, the NSO and 8BitDo 64 controllers) are mapped from `assets/controllerdb.txt`, with the C buttons as the right stick. A controller SDL doesn't know can be given a mapping in the `SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG` environment variable, which takes precedence. ## ROM hacks A ROM hack that only changes the game's assets (its audio, textures, models or text), such as an uncensored patch that restores the bleeped words, plays like the US ROM. The recompiled code only comes from the ROM's code, which has to be the US ROM's, so hacks that change the game's code are refused. A hack that repacks the game's compressed code without changing it, as the Russian fan translation does, is checked unpacked and plays too (**Version: US Russian**). The launcher's **Version** option says which ROM is in play, with its region (for example **Version: US Original** or **Version: US Uncensored**), and so does the window's title. **Add ROM** loads another: pick the hack's `.z64`, and it's put in play. After that, selecting Version switches between the ROMs you've loaded. Other regions' ROMs (such as the European one) are refused, with a message naming the region. Each is kept in `rom_versions/` in the data folder (64 MB apiece). Saves are shared between them. ## Mods Mods are `.nrm` files. Install one by copying it into the `mods` folder of the data folder above (or dropping it onto the Mods menu), then enable it in the **Mods** menu. Some mods have options there too. Each release has the included mods built, in its `Mods` zip (the same `.nrm` files work on every system). Their source is in `mods/`. Build one on Linux, macOS (which also needs `brew install llvm lld`, as Apple's clang can't compile for MIPS) or in WSL, from the repository root, after `recomp/run.sh`. It links with `ld.lld` (`sudo apt install lld`), or GNU ld (`mips-linux-gnu-ld`) where there's none, but GNU ld can't link a mod that calls the game's functions, such as Skip Intro: ```sh sh mods/build_mod.sh mods/skip_cutscenes ``` The `.nrm` ends up in the mod's `build/` folder. - **Skip Intro** (`mods/skip_intro`): boots straight to the main menu, skipping the notices, logos and the chainsaw opening. - **Skip Any Cutscene** (`mods/skip_cutscenes`): L skips a cutscene even the first time you see it. An option also allows skipping the ones the game never lets you skip. - **Cheats** (`mods/cheats`): infinite health, infinite lives and a full wallet, each toggled in the mod's options. Writing your own is covered in [recomp/README.md](recomp/README.md#mods). ### Texture packs Texture packs replace the game's textures with new ones, such as HD textures. They're RT64 texture packs, the same format as Zelda 64: Recompiled's and Banjo: Recompiled's: an `rt64.json` listing each texture's hash and its replacement image. Install a `.rtz` pack like a mod (the `mods` folder, or dropped onto the Mods menu), then pick it in **Settings > Graphics > Texture Pack**, which turns it on and the other packs off. Packs installed while the game runs are listed there from the next start. Its default, **Set in the Mods Menu**, leaves them to the **Mods** menu instead, where several can be on at once (later ones in the list take precedence). GLideN64 texture packs (for Project64 and RetroArch) work too. Install the pack's `.htc` file the same way (**Install Mods** or dropped onto the Mods menu), or put it in the `mods` folder and start the game or press the Mods menu's refresh button: it's unpacked, once, into a pack folder beside it, with its progress shown (a large pack takes a minute or so), and turned on. It's then in the **Mods** menu, and listed in **Settings > Graphics > Texture Pack**. GLideN64 names each texture by a different hash than RT64 (Rice's), which the game's RT64 works out as each texture is loaded. Only packs stored as RGBA8 are unpacked (not those built with texture compression). [`tools/texture_packs/gliden64_to_rt64.py`](tools/texture_packs/gliden64_to_rt64.py) makes a `.rtz` from a GLideN64 pack (a `.htc`, or a folder of `...#crc#format#size_all.png` files) to share: ```sh python tools/texture_packs/gliden64_to_rt64.py pack.htc --out my_pack --name "My Pack" --author Me --rtz my_pack.rtz ``` Given folders of textures dumped while playing (RT64's developer mode, below: F1, **Start dumping textures**), it instead lists the dumped textures with RT64's hashes, as RT64 without live matching needs (see the tool). To make a pack from scratch, put a folder in `mods` with a `mod.json` (`"game_id": "conker"`, plus an `id`, `version`, `display_name`, `authors` and `minimum_recomp_version`) and an `rt64.json`: ```json { "configuration": { "configurationVersion": 3, "hashVersion": 5 }, "textures": [] } ``` With it enabled, and RT64's developer mode on (`"developer_mode": true` in `graphics.json` in the data folder), RT64's inspector (F1) shows each draw's texture hash and has a **Replace** button that picks an image and adds it to the folder's `rt64.json`. Zip the folder's contents (without `mod.json`) and rename it to `.rtz` to share it. ## How it works [recomp/README.md](recomp/README.md) documents the whole pipeline: - how the decomp's ELF is prepared for N64Recomp (`recomp/prepare_elf.py`); - the recompiler configuration and hooks (`conker.toml`); - the audio microcode; - the changes to N64Recomp, N64ModernRuntime and RT64 (Conker's graphics microcode, widescreen); - the host application in `host/`; - debugging tools. ## AI assistance This project was made with heavy use of an AI coding assistant (Claude, through Claude Code). That covers the recompilation setup, the patches to the tools, the host application, the mods, and the functions decompiled to C in this repository. What's checked, and how: - **Decompiled C** is only kept when it compiles to exactly the original instructions. The build fails unless the rebuilt code is byte-for-byte identical to the ROM's. - **The port** is checked by playing it, and by comparing its behaviour with the original running in an emulator. What isn't checked: names, types and comments don't change the compiled bytes, so a byte-for-byte match says nothing about whether they're right. Names that end in an address (for example `resetSlotState_150104F0`) are best guesses based on what the code appears to do. Treat them as hints, not established facts. This is an independent project. The AI-assisted work here isn't part of the upstream decompilation, and the people behind that project and other N64 decompilation communities aren't responsible for it. Please report problems here, not to them. ## Contributing Bug reports, fixes and patches are welcome: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Credits - The [Conker's Bad Fur Day decompilation](https://github.com/mkst/conker) project, whose work this is built on. - The macOS port, and support for ROM hacks, by [nitrostemp](https://github.com/nitrostemp). - [N64Recomp](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64Recomp), [N64ModernRuntime](https://github.com/N64Recomp/N64ModernRuntime) and [RecompFrontend](https://github.com/N64Recomp/RecompFrontend) by Wiseguy and contributors. - [RT64](https://github.com/rt64/rt64) by Darío and contributors. - [ConkerBFDReloaded](https://github.com/DahSidiAbdallah/ConkerBFDReloaded) by dahmedvall95, whose widescreen pause background led to this project's. - The mod headers follow the [Banjo: Recompiled mod template](https://github.com/BanjoRecomp/BKRecompModTemplate). - Fonts: [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/), [Noto Emoji](https://fonts.google.com/noto/specimen/Noto+Emoji) and [promptfont](https://shinmera.github.io/promptfont/). ## License This project's own code is under the [MIT License](LICENSE). The submodules keep their own licenses, and a build combines them: - N64ModernRuntime (librecomp and ultramodern) is under the [GPL, version 3](tools/N64ModernRuntime/COPYING). As the program includes it, the program as a whole is distributed under the GPL version 3, which gives everyone who gets it the right to its source: this repository, at the release's tag. The release packages include the GPL's text (`LICENSE-GPL-3.0.txt`) and [`LICENSES.txt`](.github/release/LICENSES.txt), which lists them. - RT64 is under the MIT License, but the live texture pack matching that [`recomp/rt64.patch`](recomp/rt64.patch) adds (`src/hle/rt64_rice_hash.cpp`) is under the GPL, version 2 or later: it imitates the Rice texture hashing of GlideHQ (Hiroshi Morii, as in GLideN64) and Rice Video, both under the GPL version 2 or later ([recomp/README.md](recomp/README.md#local-changes-to-the-tools)). That's compatible with the GPL version 3. - The macOS linker wrapper, [`host/macos/ld64`](host/macos/ld64), which lets mods patch the program's code there, follows Banjo: Recompiled's ([github.com/BanjoRecomp/BanjoRecomp](https://github.com/BanjoRecomp/BanjoRecomp), `.github/macos/ld64`) and is under the GPL, version 3, as that is. It's only used to build, and isn't part of the program. The game itself is not included and not covered by them. Conker's Bad Fur Day is © Rare Ltd. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Rare, Microsoft or Nintendo.

releases.name: Wave Race 64 Recompiled — Aqua Water & Haptics for Windows and macOS
releases.body:
[![Watch the enhanced graphics and music showcase](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/3uaqfG4Wzcg/hqdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/3uaqfG4Wzcg)

[Watch the showcase on YouTube](https://youtu.be/3uaqfG4Wzcg).

This Windows x64 and Apple Silicon Mac update adds adjustable Aqua water and event-based controller haptics. The HD textures and replacement soundtrack are included.

## What's new

- **Aqua water is the default.** Lighter teal color and clearer shallows use the full modern rendering path, including wave interpolation, lighting, refraction, reflections, foam and wakes. Modern and Classic remain available.
- **Three Aqua sliders:** Water brightness, Aqua tint and Water clarity appear in Settings → Water when Aqua is selected. All default to 50%, preserving the reviewed preset. Press Apply to save changes.
- **Controller haptics:** distinct cues react to wave contacts, jumps and landings, collisions, crashes, correct/missed buoys, power gains, countdowns, laps and finishes. Events only is the default at 80% strength. Full adds continuous engine/water feedback; Off disables it.
- **Haptics controls and lifecycle:** strength, ambience and optional trigger vibration controls; feedback stops in pause/settings and when unfocused. Trigger vibration requires device/driver support; adaptive trigger resistance is not included.
- **Complete enhanced package:** 1,828 HD texture mappings across 1,806 images, nine replacement recordings, native rendering (Direct3D 12 on Windows, Metal on Mac) and required libraries. HD textures, Custom music and High water are enabled on a fresh install.

Existing explicit preferences and saves are preserved. To select the new look and feedback when upgrading, choose **Settings → Water → Aqua** and **Settings → Haptics → Events only**.

## macOS: download and install

Download **WaveRace64Recomp-0.4.0-macos.3-apple-silicon.zip**, extract it, and drag `WaveRace64Recomp.app` to Applications. The companion `.sha256` file verifies the download.

- Requires an **Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer), macOS 15 or later**. Intel Macs are not supported by this download. Homebrew and Xcode are not required.
- Supply your own **Wave Race 64 (USA) (Rev A / v1.1)** `.z64` in the launcher. Required SHA-1: `508dfc2d4caa42b6f6de5263d0aed5e44ac7966a`. Other revisions and regions are incompatible.
- The app is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, attempt to open it, then use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** for this app if you trust the download.
- Settings and saves remain in `~/Library/Application Support/WaveRace64Recomp`.

Keyboard controls: arrows steer, **X** accelerates, **C** is B, **Enter** is Start, and **Escape** opens settings. Controller remapping is available in the menu.

## macOS: validation and source

All **84 automated tests** passed, including settings defaults/persistence, conditional Aqua controls, haptic event envelopes, SDL output lifecycle, and bundled texture/music integrity. The renderer/runtime patches reconstruct byte-for-byte from the pinned dependencies. Native Mac testing verified DualSense motor output, a 2,301-tick haptics replay, and a 2,001-tick High/Aqua replay with clean exits. The haptics replay matched the prior physics trace at all 33 shared comparison checkpoints. The final release ZIP was extracted, its executable and bundled assets verified, and the extracted app completed a further 1,551-tick native race smoke test with a clean exit. Uploaded asset hashes match the local archive and checksum.

Testing was on an M3 Max running macOS 27. The app targets macOS 15, which has not been directly tested here. A requested 120 Hz presentation rate is not a guarantee of locked 120 FPS on every Mac or course. Full all-course playthrough coverage remains pending.

The archive contains installation instructions, `BUILD.json` with the exact source commit and executable checksum, asset manifests, dependency licenses and artwork/music credits. No ROM, original asset dumps, saves or personal settings are bundled.

[Source and build instructions](https://github.com/elliotttate/wave-race-64-recomp/tree/v0.4.0-macos.3) · [Haptics guide](https://github.com/elliotttate/wave-race-64-recomp/blob/v0.4.0-macos.3/docs/HAPTICS.md) · [Mac installation guide](https://github.com/elliotttate/wave-race-64-recomp/blob/v0.4.0-macos.3/docs/MACOS_RELEASE.md)

## Windows x64: download and install

Download **[WaveRace64Recomp-0.4.0-windows-x64.zip](https://github.com/elliotttate/wave-race-64-recomp/releases/download/v0.4.0-macos.3/WaveRace64Recomp-0.4.0-windows-x64.zip)**, extract the entire ZIP to a writable folder, and run `WaveRace64Recomp.exe`. Keep the three DLLs and `assets` folder beside the executable. Build tools and WSL are not required. The companion `.sha256` file verifies the archive; debug symbols are a separate optional download.

This new Windows build includes **adjustable Aqua water and event-based haptics**, alongside all **1,828 HD texture mappings** and **nine replacement recordings**. Fresh defaults are High/Aqua water, all three Aqua sliders at 50%, HD textures, Custom music, and Events-only haptics at 80%. Existing preferences and saves are preserved; select Aqua and Events only manually if upgrading from different settings.

Supply your own **Wave Race 64 (USA) (Rev A / v1.1)** `.z64` in the launcher (SHA-1: `508dfc2d4caa42b6f6de5263d0aed5e44ac7966a`). No ROM, original asset dumps, saves, or personal settings are included. Settings and saves remain in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\WaveRace64Recomp`. Keyboard controls are arrows, **X**, **C**, **Enter**, and **Escape**, as above.

**Windows validation:** on an RTX 5090 using Direct3D 12, a fresh-settings High/Aqua Sunny Beach replay completed 2,000 ticks and exited cleanly. All 49 game-state checkpoints through tick 1410 matched the previous Windows build's Original-water replay. Audio capture confirmed game audio and replacement music mixing. Haptics traces recorded game events and nonzero motor levels. Fifteen focused tests, the Windows-native SDL virtual-controller output test, all 32 DXIL/SPIR-V shader compilations, patch reconstruction, and package integrity checks passed. Physical controller feedback and feel have not been verified here. Windows Vulkan playback, other GPU families, and full all-course coverage remain untested.

The ZIP includes `INSTALLATION.md`, `BUILD.json` with exact source and executable checksums, manifests, and credits. [Windows source: `9041cc8`](https://github.com/elliotttate/wave-race-64-recomp/tree/v0.4.0-windows.2) · [Windows installation and validation](https://github.com/elliotttate/wave-race-64-recomp/blob/v0.4.0-windows.2/docs/WINDOWS_RELEASE.md) · [Windows build instructions](https://github.com/elliotttate/wave-race-64-recomp/blob/v0.4.0-windows.2/docs/BUILDING.md) · [Haptics guide](https://github.com/elliotttate/wave-race-64-recomp/blob/v0.4.0-windows.2/docs/HAPTICS.md)

## Windows x64: download and install

Download **[WaveRace64Recomp-0.4.0-windows-x64.zip](https://github.com/elliotttate/wave-race-64-recomp/releases/download/v0.4.0-macos.2/WaveRace64Recomp-0.4.0-windows-x64.zip)**, extract the entire ZIP to a writable folder, and run `WaveRace64Recomp.exe`. Keep the three DLLs and `assets` folder beside the executable. Build tools and WSL are not required to play. The companion `.sha256` file verifies the archive; debug symbols are an optional separate download.

- Includes all **1,828 HD texture mappings across 1,806 images**, **nine replacement recordings**, and **High/Modern water**, enabled on a fresh install. Credits and manifests are bundled. Saved preferences are preserved when upgrading.
- Native Windows x64 build with Direct3D 12 rendering. Supply your own **Wave Race 64 (USA) (Rev A / v1.1)** `.z64` in the launcher. Required SHA-1: `508dfc2d4caa42b6f6de5263d0aed5e44ac7966a`. No ROM, original asset dumps, saves, or personal settings are included.
- Fixes the Direct3D 12 water pipeline root signature that could cause a crash on the first enhanced-water draw, and corrects CPU/RSP source generation for Windows builds.
- Keyboard defaults: arrows steer, **X** accelerates, **C** is B, **Enter** is Start, and **Escape** opens settings. Controller remapping is available in the launcher. Settings and saves live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\WaveRace64Recomp`.

**Windows validation:** an RTX 5090 Direct3D 12 Sunny Beach Time Trial replay with HD textures, Custom music, High water, and Modern appearance completed 1,800 ticks and exited cleanly. All 49 game-state checkpoints through tick 1410 matched the Original-water replay. Captured audio verified game audio and replacement music mixing. All 32 DXIL/SPIR-V water shader compilations, nine bundled-asset tests, four default-setting tests, patch reconstruction, and package integrity checks passed. This is startup/race smoke coverage; all-course playthroughs, Windows Vulkan playback, and other GPU families remain untested here.
