Multiplayer packages expose separate player cards in the launcher. Keyboard and gamepads can be assigned independently, including keyboard + controller. The F1 controller-port option swaps existing host assignments between PlayStation ports; it does not select physical devices. ## Release-wide limitations - **F1 → Display → Window Scale does not work reliably.** Window Scale is separate from internal rendering resolution and does not control supersampling. Close the game and use the pre-launch GUI to change supersampling. - Local multiplayer metadata is included, but representative Player 2 testing remains unqualified. - Most titles have an automated startup-survival pass, not an end-to-end game completion claim. Read the selected release notes and any included `COMPATIBILITY.md`. - Performance has not been profiled across representative desktop and laptop hardware. - Locally built executables are not digitally signed and may trigger Windows SmartScreen. - `setup.log`, `settings.toml`, and runtime report JSON files can contain local filesystem paths. Redact them before attaching them to a public issue. ## Contributing Anyone may fork this repository and study or experiment with the build kits for noncommercial purposes, subject to this repository's PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0, PSXRecomp's license, and the rights applicable to each original game. Contributions and reproducible compatibility reports are welcome. Report problems through **Issues** using this title format: `[Game Name][Issue] Short description` For example: `[Alien Resurrection][Issue] Intro FMV displays a corrupted band`. Include the release version, game region/serial, point reached in gameplay, reproduction steps, expected behavior, and observed behavior. Do not upload game media, BIOS files, generated game or BIOS code, locally built executables, memory cards, save states, or unredacted local paths. ## About this project These ports are developed by a hobbyist (a DevSecOps engineer, not a game programmer) with substantial AI assistance. What keeps that honest: every change is validated before it ships - boot gates, hardware-oracle A/B comparisons (Beetle/DuckStation), deterministic replay probes, and a shared findings registry that documents failures as carefully as successes. AI writes most of the code; the evidence discipline decides what survives. Bug reports welcome - expect them to be investigated the same way. tl;dr AI writes the code, but I always test it myself before pushing These projects are powered by [`psxrecomp`](https://github.com/mstan/psxrecomp), licensed under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. Game names identify compatibility targets only. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or any game publisher or developer.

metadata.name: SSX3-recomp
metadata.description: Static recompilation of SSX 3 (original Xbox, PAL) into a native Windows program

readme_text:
# ssx3-recomp

Static recompilation of **SSX 3** (original Xbox, PAL) into a native Windows
program, built with [xboxrecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp).
The game's own code runs as native x86-64, and the Xbox GPU is emulated on
Vulkan. It plays at **60 FPS**, at your monitor's resolution, in **true
widescreen** (16:9, 21:9 or 32:9).

![Snow Jam in 32:9 at 5120x1440](docs/screenshots/33-widescreen-32x9-snow-jam.png)
<sub>Snow Jam on a 5120x1440 (32:9) monitor: the game's camera is widened, so nothing is stretched, and the HUD keeps its shape.</sub>

No game data or game code is in this repository. You need your own rip of the
disc (`default.xbe` + `data/`); everything derived from it is regenerated by
the scripts below.

## What works

- **The whole game.** Boot, menus, every Race and Freestyle event on all
  three peaks, Conquer the Mountain (free-roam, transport), and
  2-player split-screen with two controllers.
- **Saving and loading.** Saves go to a hard-disk save in `game\UDATA`,
  and local time zones are respected.
- **60 FPS.** The game's vertex programs and pixel combiners run on the GPU.
  A 2-hour automated soak test passed with no crash, and 48 of 48 parallel
  boots reached a race.
- **Accurate visuals**, checked frame by frame against the
  [xemu](https://xemu.app) emulator: lighting, colours, snow spray,
  board trails and the display gamma ramp.
- **Modern display.** The game renders at your monitor's height (1440p, 4K,
  ...) in your monitor's shape. Fullscreen is F11 or Alt+Enter.
- **Audio** through the emulated Xbox sound chip, plus rumble on an XInput
  controller.
- **Keyboard and controller**, with remappable keys and buttons
  (`keys.ini`).

## What's new

| | |
|---|---|
| **True widescreen.** The game's camera projection (D3DX `PerspectiveFovLH`) is widened to your monitor's aspect, so you see more of the mountain instead of a stretched picture. The HUD keeps its 4:3 proportions, and menus are pillarboxed. | ![16:9](docs/screenshots/34-widescreen-16x9-snow-jam.png) |
| **Native resolution.** The Vulkan renderer draws at your monitor's height (5120x1440 above, 1920x1080 here) and hands the full image to the window. The game itself still sees 640x480. | ![1080p](docs/screenshots/38-character-select-1080p.png) |
| **Lighting matches the hardware.** Riders were washed out because vertex colours were not clamped the way the Xbox GPU clamps them. Left: xemu; right: this project. | ![lighting](docs/screenshots/39-lighting-vs-xemu.png) |
| **Every peak.** All Peak 2 and 3 races (Ruthless Ridge, Intimidator, Ruthless, Gravitude, The Throne) and the Freestyle events on every peak load and run. | ![peaks](docs/screenshots/40-peaks-2-3-races.png) |
| **Freestyle**: halfpipe, slopestyle, big air and the night event with fireworks. | ![freestyle](docs/screenshots/41-freestyle-all-peaks.png) |
| **Trails and snow spray.** The game draws board trails as lines and snow spray as point sprites. The GPU renderer now draws both, following xemu's rules. | ![trails](docs/screenshots/42-intimidator-board-trails.png) |
| **2-player split-screen** (Multi Play) works when two controllers are plugged in at start. | ![split](docs/screenshots/43-split-screen.png) |
| **Conquer the Mountain** free-roam and stations, in widescreen. | ![ctm](docs/screenshots/36-widescreen-conquer-the-mountain.png) |
| **Race briefing**: the 3D scene fills the screen and the panel stays centred. | ![briefing](docs/screenshots/35-widescreen-briefing.png) |
| **Menus** keep their 4:3 artwork, pillarboxed. | ![menu](docs/screenshots/37-menu-pillarboxed.png) |

Other new things:

- **Windows-only build path.** No WSL is needed: `setup.ps1`, `regen.ps1`
  and `build.bat`, verified from a fresh clone.
- **Test tooling.**
  - The game can drive its own menus (`RECOMP_AUTONAV`), getting from boot
    to a race in about 27 s.
  - Every scripted run gets its own save (with everything unlocked) and its
    own emulated hard disk.
- **xemu as a reference.** `tools\xemu.ps1` and the `xemu` agent skill boot
  xemu with the ISO, press buttons, capture frames, restore snapshots
  (character select, race start, ...) in a second and read the game's frame
  counter.

## Play

On Windows, after building:

```
tools\play.bat
```

No settings are needed. The defaults follow your monitor. The optional
settings are environment variables:

| Setting | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `RECOMP_WIDESCREEN` | `auto` | `auto` = the window's shape (your monitor's at start, then follows resizes); `16:9`, `21:9`, any `W:H`; `0` = original 4:3 |
| `RECOMP_RES` | monitor height | internal resolution as a height (`1080`, `1440`, `2160`) or `480` for the original |
| `RECOMP_SKIP_INTRO` | `1` | `0` plays the EA/THX/intro movies |
| `RECOMP_GPU` | Vulkan | `sw` = the software rasteriser (reference/fallback) |
| `RECOMP_PRESENT_FILTER` | linear | `point` for sharp pixels |

**Keyboard.** The game window must have focus. Remap the keys by copying
`keys.example.ini` to `keys.ini` and editing it.

| Key | Pad | Key | Pad |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | Start | Backspace | Back |
| Z X A S | A B X Y | Q E | White / Black |
| 1 3 | Left / right trigger | Arrows | D-pad |
| Numpad 8/4/2/6 | Left stick | I J K L | Right stick |
| F11 / Alt+Enter | Fullscreen | | |

**Controller.** An Xbox/XInput controller works without setup, rumble
included; two controllers enable Multi Play. Each run's log is kept in
`logs\`. A crash also leaves a minidump there (`crash_<time>.dmp`, open it
in Visual Studio next to `build\ssx3_recomp.pdb`).

## Build

**Windows** (no WSL). You need Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ workload,
the Vulkan SDK (`winget install KhronosGroup.VulkanSDK`), git and
Python 3.9+.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/koenhendriks/SSX3-recomp.git ssx3-recomp; cd ssx3-recomp
# put your rip in game\ : game\default.xbe and game\data\
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\setup.ps1   # toolkit (pinned + patched) in ..\xboxrecomp, Python venv
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\regen.ps1   # analysis, decomp\ split, src\recomp\gen\ C lift (~7 min)
tools\build.bat                                              # MSVC + Ninja, ~2 min on 32 threads
tools\play.bat
```

**From WSL**, which is how the project is developed. The build itself is the
same MSVC build on the Windows side:

```bash
scripts/setup.sh                 # toolkit clone (pinned + patched) and Python venv
scripts/regen.sh                 # needs the rip in ../SSX3/
scripts/sync-windows.sh --game   # copy to C:\Code\Xbox for the MSVC build
cmd.exe /c 'C:\Code\Xbox\ssx3-recomp\tools\build.bat'
```

The toolkit is pinned at v0.13.1 (`193e299`), with this project's fixes in
`patches/xboxrecomp-local.patch`. For Linux, see docs/LINUX.md.

## Testing

Scripted runs are silent, ignore a real controller, render at 640x480 in
4:3, and each gets its own copy of a save fixture, so your saves are never
touched and the PC stays usable while they run. The fixture is
`work\saves\unlocked\` (not in git): copy your `game\UDATA` there,
ideally from a save with every peak unlocked; without it runs start with
no save. Run these from the repo root on Windows:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `tools\race_test.ps1 -Runs 1 -RaceSec 20 -Snap x.png [-Rider N -Peak N -Mode N -Event N]` | boot to a race, ride, screenshot |
| `tools\race_par.ps1 -Instances 8 -Runs 3` | parallel boot-to-race batches (24 runs in ~3 min) |
| `tools\cycle_test.ps1 -Cycles 12` | race, pause, quit to the title, again (leak/soak) |
| `tools\menu_test.ps1 -Steps "y,wait,down,a"` | menu presses with a screenshot per step (`p2-a` for player 2) |
| `tools\burst.ps1 -From 15 -To 40 -Every 2` | screenshot burst during a race |
| `tools\bench.ps1 -Seconds 60 -Peak N -Event N` | frame-time benchmark (`logs\bench_*.json`) |
| `tools\xemu.ps1 start -Snapshot race_go -Paused` / `cap` / `press` | reference frames from xemu |

## Known issues

- **Effects DSP.** The game's audio effects processor (reverb etc.) is a
  stub, so there is no reverb. The level meter shows sound in races, menus
  and the intro movies.
- **Metro-City's tunnel** drops to 30 FPS. The game does that itself: xemu
  drops at the same point.
- **Peaks 2 and 3** are locked on a fresh save, as in the original game.
  Unlock them in game or with the cheat.
- **Untested.** Audio hasn't been checked by ear in every mode.

## Screenshots of the journey

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| ![](docs/screenshots/01-black-window-no-draws.png) | ![](docs/screenshots/05-intro-movie.png) | ![](docs/screenshots/12-gameplay-race.png) |
| first boot: a black window | the intro movie plays | first race (software renderer, ~5 FPS) |
| ![](docs/screenshots/21-race-async-11fps.png) | ![](docs/screenshots/27-vulkan-race-57fps.png) | ![](docs/screenshots/29-metro-city-60fps.png) |
| asynchronous GPU executor, 11 FPS | Vulkan renderer, 57 FPS | Metro-City at 60 FPS |
| ![](docs/screenshots/17-title-screen.png) | ![](docs/screenshots/30-equip-gear.png) | ![](docs/screenshots/31-load-game.png) |
| title screen | Equip Gear | loading a hard-disk save |

## Legal

This is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by
Electronic Arts or Microsoft. SSX and SSX 3 are trademarks of Electronic
Arts. The repository holds only original code, tooling and notes: no game
code, data or assets. The build is generated from a copy of the game you
own, and the screenshots show this project running.

## License

GPL-2.0-or-later (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)), copyright Koen Hendriks and
Corné Dorrestijn. One exception: `patches/xboxrecomp-local.patch` changes
the [xboxrecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp) toolkit and is
offered under the toolkit's own licenses (MIT, and LGPL-2.1 for its APU
files), so the fixes can go upstream.

## More

- [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md): the plan and tracker (phases, gates,
  progress log).
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): the bring-up history, every fix, the debugging
  workflow and the open investigations.
- [docs/VULKAN.html](docs/VULKAN.html) and [docs/LINUX.md](docs/LINUX.md):
  the Vulkan renderer and the Linux port, by Corné Dorrestijn.

metadata.name: mm3-recomp
metadata.description: Experimental, largely AI-written static recompilation of Midtown Madness 3 for Windows. Expect rough edges; fixes and PRs welcome.

readme_text:
> **AI-generated code warning:** Nearly all project code was written with AI assistance.
> Expect bugs and rough edges. Reviews, fixes and improvements are welcome.

# Midtown Madness 3 recompilation

Experimental static recompilation of the Xbox game to native x86-64 Windows,
using [xboxrecomp](tools/xboxrecomp) and Direct3D 11. Build it from your own
supported game disc; game assets are not included.

This combines [Matt Graham's project](https://github.com/MattSG/mm3-recomp)
with the car tools, gameplay repairs and runtime improvements contributed from
[lakshya16157's PC Native fork](https://github.com/lakshya16157/midtown-madness-3-PC-Native).
The contributions were prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The
[integration record](docs/integration-2026-10-13.md) records preserved features,
source revisions, validation and remaining gameplay coverage.

Generic improvements in our fork that could help other original Xbox game
recompilations should eventually be tidied up, tested, and submitted as focused
PRs to [upstream XboxRecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp). Keep
MM3-specific hooks and workarounds in this repository.

The runtime derives from [MattSG/xboxrecomp](https://github.com/MattSG/xboxrecomp),
a fork of [sp00nznet/xboxrecomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp).
This is an unofficial community project with no affiliation with Microsoft,
Xbox or Digital Illusions CE (DICE).

## Features

The combined source retains upstream's Settings, Controls and Mods launcher,
configurable keyboard/mouse and controller bindings, menu mouse navigation,
intro skipping, required collision-cell repair and console-rate simulation.
The [mod registry](src/mods/mods.c) lists its switches and defaults; required
collision and disc-authentication repairs remain enabled.

The fork adds nine extra-car identities and a standalone Car Workshop editor,
MM2/MM1 exterior conversion, source credits, model/shadow/light/reflection/menu
artwork repair, donor-based driving defaults, analog gauge handling, map zoom,
checkpoint alignment and road-following race guidance. Its runtime work covers
shader caches/prewarming, texture and surface synchronization, presentation
pacing, audio processing and guest memory/handle/fence repairs. Integration
checks for these features are tracked separately in the
[preservation matrix](docs/integration-2026-10-13.md#feature-preservation).

Matt's System Link and Insignia DNS changes are retained. Upstream verified
System Link between copies on one PC; this combined feature bundle still needs
multiplayer gameplay verification. Xbox Live sign-in remains unverified. To
import an account created in xemu, use
`py scripts/import_xemu_accounts.py <xbox_hdd.qcow2> <save dir>` and provide that
console's keys through `RECOMP_XBOX_HDKEY`, `RECOMP_XBOX_SIGKEY` and
`RECOMP_XBOX_LANKEY` (32 hexadecimal digits each). Keep accounts and keys local.

For two script-launched instances on one PC, use a separate PowerShell session
and a different save directory for each player:

```powershell
$env:MM3_SAVE_DIR = 'C:\MM3\player-one' # use player-two in the other session
pwsh scripts/play.ps1 -AllowMultipleInstances
```

The script refuses two launches using the same save directory. Normal launches
retain the single-instance guard. Launch metadata redacts console keys while
the game still receives their environment values.

## Build and play

You need Windows 10/11 x64, Visual Studio 2022 or newer with **Desktop development with C++**
(it includes CMake), Python 3.12+ recommended (3.11.4+ supported), git,
and your own Midtown Madness 3 disc.
Examples use PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`). Install it separately or use the portable
PowerShell under `tools/bin/powershell` when it is available.
Initial CMake configuration downloads pinned FreeType 2.13.3 and RmlUi 6.3 for
the settings launcher, so a fresh configure requires network access.

```powershell
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/MattSG/mm3-recomp.git
cd mm3-recomp
pwsh scripts\setup.ps1 -Iso "D:\Games\Midtown Madness 3 (USA).iso"
.\build\RelWithDebInfo\mm3_recomp.exe  # opens Settings, Controls and Mods
```

`setup.ps1` checks the toolchain, makes `tools\venv` with tested Capstone 5.0.7, verifies the disc and
extracts it to `game_files\`, generates the translated C into `src\recomp\gen\` (about six
minutes, deterministic) and builds `build\RelWithDebInfo\mm3_recomp.exe`. Re-running skips
finished steps; `-Force` redoes them. Nothing from the disc is committed.

The runtime fixes from the PC Native fork live in the pinned `tools/xboxrecomp`
submodule commit; `git submodule update --init --recursive` fetches them.

For a checkout with local tools installed, activate them in the current PowerShell session:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass -Force
. .\scripts\enter-env.ps1
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\setup.ps1 -Iso "D:\Games\Midtown Madness 3 (USA).iso"
```

The local environment uses `tools\venv`, portable PowerShell at `tools\bin\powershell`,
and MSVC/Windows SDK at `tools\bin\msvc` (via `setup_x64.bat`). With local MSVC,
install CMake and Ninja in the venv (`python -m pip install "cmake>=3.20,<4" ninja`);
setup uses Ninja Multi-Config and keeps the same `build\<Config>` output paths.
Run these commands from the repository directory, not its parent folder.

Generated Xbox translations and game assets stay local. Setup validates and extracts
your own disc; compiled game code and source-model downloads are not bundled.
The runtime commit is pinned by the submodule and the additional patch is
version-specific. See the integration record before moving that pin manually.

### Which disc

Any dump whose `default.xbe` carries the retail code: a redump `.iso` (video + game partitions)
or a bare XISO. `scripts\extract_disc.py` gates on a SHA-256 of the XBE's section data
(`9c437324…6bbf8ba4`) with the one byte XISO tools patch to skip the DVD media check
(VA `0x87226`, `jge` → `jmp`) normalised, so region/certificate differences and that patch do
not matter. USA and Europe/Australia share the same code. Extraction applies that same media
patch to `game_files\default.xbe` (the emulated drive can't authenticate a pressed disc), so every
supported disc translates identically. Images tested end to end:

| SHA-1 | Image |
|---|---|
| `52cd998731eb67477b44c49c4152f56c0fc58a56` | Midtown Madness 3 (USA) — redump `.iso`, 7.8 GB |
| `8ed003adaf504883afc980d2888df6125496d044` | Midtown Madness 3 (Europe, Australia) (En,Fr,De,Es,It) — XISO, 3.6 GB |

An untested image with matching code is accepted with a note; anything else is refused with
this list.

### Regenerating

Use `scripts\generate_mm3.py` for regeneration. The supported recipe uses the
recompiler pinned to toolkit commit `967ec30`, extracted to `tools\.generator\`.
That generator pin is separate from the runtime submodule pin. Changing
`MM3_GENERATOR_DIR` selects a different generator and requires translation and
gameplay validation; the integration does not establish that arbitrary regenerated
output is compatible with the game's native hooks.

An existing pre-integration checkout with old files in `src\recomp\gen\` must
regenerate once for the integrated hooks. Fresh-clone setup generates them
automatically; setup otherwise skips an existing generated directory. Run the
generator directly, then rerun setup to build:

```powershell
. .\scripts\enter-env.ps1
python -m pip install capstone==5.0.7
python scripts\generate_mm3.py
pwsh scripts\setup.ps1
```

This replaces local translated code while keeping the existing `game_files\`
and installed car assets. Use this procedure without `setup.ps1 -Force`, which
also re-extracts the game files. A checkout already populated with the tested
integrated generated files is ready to build without regenerating again.

## Launcher and controls

Starting the executable normally opens the **Settings**, **Controls**, and
**Mods** launcher. Settings save to `mm3_settings.ini` beside `game_files/` when
you press Play. Keyboard and controller bindings are configurable there.

- **Launcher:** Enter plays, Esc quits; arrows, Space, and Tab navigate.
  A controller also works: D-pad/stick to navigate, A to change, LB/RB for tabs,
  Start to play, and Back to quit.
- **Keyboard play:** enable keyboard and mouse under Controls. Defaults include
  arrows for D-pad, Z/X/A/S for A/B/X/Y, Enter for Start, Backspace for Back,
  and numpad 8/2/4/6 for the left stick.
- **Menu mouse:** enable menu keys and mouse under Controls. Point to select,
  click or Space to confirm, and right-click or Esc to go back.
- **Fullscreen:** F11 or Alt+Enter toggles it in game.

For a direct launch that skips the settings window:

```powershell
pwsh scripts/play.ps1 -Keyboard -Profile Balanced
```

The world updates at a fixed tick rate whatever the frame rate: 30 (the Xbox's),
60 (the default) or 90 a second under Settings > Tick rate. Handling, speed and
the race AI are the same at any frame rate. Frames between updates show the last
one again; Settings > **Draw every frame** (`MM3_RENDER_EVERY_FRAME=1`) renders
them anyway, with the one-frame effects (menu text, tail lights) restored. Lower
supersampling or internal resolution if performance is poor.

Profiles are applied before the settings launcher so saved Auto resolution,
aspect and FOV selections can take effect. The launcher includes 16:10 aspect
and 720p internal rendering in addition to upstream's choices.

The launcher saves custom mappings; [input runtime](tools/xboxrecomp/src/input)
implements them. The fork's gameplay aliases and focus handling are preserved
in the integration target, with their precedence against saved mappings
tracked in the validation matrix. To select custom cars and model packages,
use the separate Workshop described below.

## Fork gameplay options

The fork's MM3 keyboard layout provides arrow-key driving, C to change camera,
Space for handbrake and R/F for manual shifting while driving. Ctrl enlarges the
race map; its checkpoint markers remain aligned and the road-following route
updates toward the next checkpoint. Saved launcher bindings can customize input;
use the integration record for verification of remapping and default aliases.

The closest chase camera retains its 0.25 m adjustment. Driving FOV and draw
settings are available through the launcher. Direct launches retain these options:

```powershell
pwsh scripts/play.ps1 -Profile Balanced -Keyboard -Fullscreen -Fov 100 -FpsLimit 60
```

`-Profile` accepts Balanced, Quality or LowPower. `-Fov` accepts 60–110 degrees
of absolute horizontal driving FOV. `-TraceBuildings` enables focused diagnostics;
`-NoTraceBuildings` disables them. Normal play leaves focused tracing off.
The script preserves its logged launch settings and explicit environment overrides.

The original 35 cars keep their earned availability rules. `MM3_UNLOCK_ALL_CARS=1`
makes installed cars selectable without writing unlock keys to a profile.
`MM3_SAVE_DIR` selects an isolated UDATA/TDATA save root for test builds. Close
MM3 before applying Workshop changes and keep a copy of your normal saves when
trying an integrated build.

## Added cars and editing stats

The optional [extra-car pack](tools/car-mods/README.md) adds nine separately
selectable slots alongside the 35 original cars:
Panoz GTR-1, McLaren F1, Formula 1, Ford GT,
McLaren Senna, McLaren Senna GTR, Ferrari FXX K, Koenigsegg Regera and Lamborghini
Aventador. Each has its own name, paint settings, menu ratings and driving setup.
The [model names, download sources and creator credits](tools/car-models/README.md#extra-car-names-and-model-credits)
identify each imported exterior and its original conversion pack.
The remaining slots retain their IDs. Profiles that remember a removed custom
car use its original donor vehicle, without restoring the removed menu entry.

The supplied defaults use stock donor visuals. Workshop's **Model** tab can
select prepared imported body, wheel, texture and selection-artwork packages; reapplying
stats preserves that selection. The [model workflow](tools/car-models/README.md)
documents the verified Panoz, F1 GTR, Ferrari F2007, Ford GT, Senna, Senna GTR,
FXX K, Regera and Aventador conversions. Downloaded models and generated packages
are not distributed in this repository. Imported initial liveries remain fixed,
glass is opaque, and interior, sounds and collision remain based on the donor.
The [menu-artwork repair](tools/car-models/README.md#repair-selection-menu-artwork-in-already-prepared-packages)
regenerates selection icons and blue backgrounds from each package's source
exterior, with backups. The preview and repair tools require NumPy and Pillow;
building new model packages also requires SciPy. Close MM3, repair the selected
packages, then reapply the matching Workshop manifest to install the new artwork.
Roadside trees fall in the impact direction at or above 18 km/h, retaining
native impact sounds and effects while clearing the struck tree's collision.
Defaults retain the donor's engine curve, automatic shifting, gearbox and
handling. Only mass and native torque scale are tuned for arcade driving.
Manufacturer specifications remain available as references in Workshop.

### Visual editor

1. Close the game, then double-click [tools/car-mods/editor.cmd](tools/car-mods/editor.cmd)
   or run `tools\car-mods\editor.cmd` from the repository root.
2. Select an added car. **Car specs** shows its reference variant, source links
   and calibration notes; **Restore default driving** restores the weight/power
   preset while retaining paint, ratings, gauges and model choices. Edit its paint, menu ratings, physics, gearing, RPM
   settings and interior speedometer ranges. Blank optional physics fields inherit
   the stock donor's settings.
3. Choose **Save** to write the selected manifest, or **Save & Apply**
   to save and install the changes into your extracted `game_files` data.
4. Restart the game and select the car to load the changes.

The paint view is a schematic color preview; it does not display or edit the 3D
car mesh. The editor is a small Python/Tkinter desktop app with no web server or
extra GUI packages. Its source is [editor.py](tools/car-mods/editor.py).

### JSON and command-line editing

The editor and installer select `tools/car-mods/cars.local.json` when present,
otherwise [tools/car-mods/cars.json](tools/car-mods/cars.json). The local file is
ignored by Git and keeps machine-specific model selections and tuning. Copy the
tracked defaults to `cars.local.json` to start local settings on a fresh checkout.
You can edit the selected file directly with a text editor. From the repository
root, run the preview first, then apply with
the game closed:

```powershell
tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\car-mods\prepare.py
tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\car-mods\prepare.py --apply
pwsh scripts\play.ps1 -Keyboard
```

Both the editor and installer accept `--config <path>` and `--game-dir <path>`
for another manifest or extracted game directory. For example:

```powershell
tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\car-mods\editor.py --config tools\car-mods\cars.json --game-dir game_files
tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\car-mods\prepare.py --config tools\car-mods\cars.json --game-dir game_files --apply
```

Keep `id`, `alias`, `donor` and `display_name` unchanged: these identities are
registered by the runtime. Adding a new identity or donor body requires code
changes as well as a manifest entry. The supplied editor and manifest tune the
added variants; they do not provide a general editor for every original car.

### What each setting changes

Menu ratings are integers from 0 to 9: `TOPSPEED`, `ACCELERATION`, `MASS`,
`HANDLING` and `DURABILITY`. They control the menu bars. Actual driving behavior
comes from the separate `physics` settings, and `colors` contains one to three
paint colors in `#rrggbb` format.

| Physics setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| `TorqueScale`, `TorqueScaleFactor` | Peak torque in Nm with a factory profile, or donor torque scale; its multiplier. |
| `Mass` | Physical weight. |
| `BrakeTorque`, `HandBrakeTorque` | Braking and handbrake strength. |
| `LatFrictionFactor` | Cornering grip. |
| `AirKZZ`, `AirKZY` | Aerodynamic coefficients. |
| `WheelDrive` | 0: front wheels; 1: rear wheels; 2: all wheels. |
| `SteeringEndSpeed` | Speed-dependent steering setting. |
| `WheelRadius` | Wheel radius, also used in automatic shift-speed calculations. |
| `GearRatioVector` | Reverse ratio followed by one through seven forward ratios. |
| `WheelRatio` | Final drive multiplier; a smaller value makes gears longer. |
| `TimeChangeGear`, `TimeChangeGearFR` | Forward shifting and forward/reverse transition times, in seconds. |
| `MinRPM`, `MinRPMGearChange`, `CutRPM`, `MaxRPM` | Idle, minimum shift, cutoff and redline settings. |
| `MaxTorqueRPM`, `MaxTurboTorqueRPM` | Peak torque RPM references; automatic shift target in donor mode. |
| `GearStatusDownGearFactor` | Automatic downshift factor. |

For example, changing Panoz's `physics.TorqueScale` from `750` to `800`
increases engine torque. Changing `ratings.ACCELERATION` changes only its menu bar.
The installer validates supported value ranges before applying changes.

### Gearing and speedometers

Use a negative reverse ratio followed by positive, decreasing forward ratios,
for example `[-3.3, 2.5, 1.72, 1.28, 1.0, 0.82, 0.7]`. Gear count is derived
from this array; do not add `NGears`. Keep
`MinRPM < MinRPMGearChange < CutRPM <= MaxRPM`, and keep both peak-torque RPM
settings above idle and below cutoff. Donor mode retains the stock torque curve's
8,000 RPM peak limit. The supplied presets leave the donor's gear ratios,
final drive, RPM limits and shift times unchanged. Formula 1 uses the Lotus
five-speed gearbox; McLaren F1 and Regera use the Koenigsegg six-speed gearbox.
The optional advanced `engine_profile: "factory"` mode remains available for
experiments with researched curves and transmissions; it is disabled in the
default and imported presets.

Automatic upshifts depend on road speed calculated from gear ratios, final drive,
wheel radius and the factory profile's shift target, or peak torque RPM in donor
mode (the turbo peak for a turbo-equipped donor).
Wheelspin can raise RPM before the car reaches its shift speed. Lowering
`MinRPMGearChange` alone does not make automatic upshifts happen earlier.
The default presets restore the stock shifting behavior, and the installer
rejects conflicting thresholds in custom edits. Select **Automatic** or **Manual**
in the game's car setup; Manual uses **R/F** on the MM3 keyboard layout or Xbox
**B/X** to shift up/down while driving.

The optional `speedometer.max_kmh` and `speedometer.max_mph` values set an added
car's interior dashboard needle range. Its on-screen speedometer keeps the
donor's native font, artwork, gauge style and scale. Interior ranges provide
rounded headroom for each preset: **360 km/h / 240 mph** for Panoz through
**440 km/h / 280 mph** for Regera. Enter both limits, or leave both blank in the
editor to inherit the donor interior gauge. These limits change the interior
needle range, not engine power, actual top speed or the `TOPSPEED` menu rating. In the workshop, use
**Original car speedometers…** to change original sport and Koenigsegg HUDs.
Koenigsegg, Viper and Lotus default to 800 km/h / 500 mph. Their original physics
and interior gauges stay unchanged. Blank original limits restore the retail HUD.
The numeric speed readout is hidden in every HUD layout; analog dials and
their native styles remain active. Original-car HUD overrides remain available.

The installer backs up affected game archives and reuses those originals when
reapplying, so edits do not accumulate. It does not edit saved profiles. To
remove the pack and restore the original game data, close the game and run:

```powershell
tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\car-mods\prepare.py --restore
```

## Development and validation

The latest submission passed fresh full generation, an independent MSVC build,
hidden launcher rendering/normal close, both rendering-mode contracts and scoped
car/map/runtime checks. Detailed current results and skipped coverage appear at
the beginning of [the integration record](docs/integration-2026-10-13.md).
Fresh driving and multiplayer acceptance remain unverified.

The preceding integration's car/model/factory/import tests ran **135 cases**:
**129 passed and six skipped** because optional local fixtures, decoder oracle
or symbolic-link privileges were unavailable. Corrected simulation tests passed
18 timing/ABI and 16 actual generated-loop cases, including a frozen-cadence
negative control. Runtime validation passed 198 CTest cases across
19 suites and its MSVC build. Eight harmless play-script profile/logging tests,
nine production launcher settings-helper cases and fresh-generated native
camera/map/route/HUD/input/car/collision/translation contracts also passed.
That preceding combined game build, launcher smoke and Paris driving checks
passed before the latest networking and render-tihttps://github.com/MattSG/mm3-recomp/pull/6/conflict?name=README.md&ancestor_oid=81825769dcd5e746dcb316227774df4cbd2aa9c5&base_oid=81c670d2c87eb7eeca9070e3750a1e8b24c0e430&head_oid=41f380b22a0a492008a1f95d014cdf1f6a6a3948ck changes. Independent guest/world-clock traces verified the default
30 Hz world rate at both requested render limits. Actual driving medians were
59.96 FPS with 60 requested and 71.52 FPS (about 72) with 90 requested. These
were direction/acceleration checks; achieved 90 FPS, real-race 60 Hz simulation
and matched handling parity remain extended coverage. See the integration
record for scope and measurements.

- [Integration record](docs/integration-2026-10-13.md): preserved features, source boundaries, tests and remaining acceptance work.
- [Setup](scripts/setup.ps1) and [generator](scripts/generate_mm3.py): supported extraction, translation and build recipe.
- [Launcher](src/mm3_launcher.cpp) and [mod registry](src/mods/mods.c): settings, defaults and environment mappings.
- [Runtime](tools/xboxrecomp): renderer, audio, input, threading and fork fixes.
- [Developer tools](tools/debug-features/README.md), [teleport debugger](DEBUG_TELEPORT.md) and [custom-menu investigation](CUSTOM_MENUS.md).
- [Historical fork reference](docs/fork-reference-2026-10-13.md): previous runtime pin, profiles, performance measurements, diagnostic flags and October 12 upstream comparison.
- [Historical integration backlog](Next%20fixes%20to%20do.txt): earlier missing-fix evidence; its statuses are not a current audit of the merged source.
- [Third-party licences](THIRD_PARTY.md) and [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md).

PRs should address one problem and include the checks actually run. AI-assisted
contributions are welcome; review their code and provenance. Runtime changes
belong in the runtime repository, with corresponding game-side integration when
needed. A source merge or test pass does not replace menu, driving, race and
save/reload acceptance on the combined executable.

## Features and limits

The launcher exposes widescreen, extended draw distance, skyline filtering,
field of view, menu mouse support, intro skipping, console-rate simulation, and
offline-network bypass.
Optional developer tools and a teleport debugger are also available. The
[mod registry](src/mods/mods.c) lists their switches and defaults.

Audio runs the Xbox's sound DSP as on the console: reverb, 3D sound and the
game's own mix. Its programs are recompiled to native code: the first time
you play, the game saves them to `game_files\dsp` (`[DSP] GP program saved`
in the log), and the next build compiles them in. Until then an interpreter
runs them, which needs about half as much CPU again. If sound stutters
(`[XA2] underrun` in the log), set the launcher's Audio > Sound processor to
Off (`RECOMP_APU_DSP=0`): the voices are mixed directly at a fraction of the
CPU, without those effects, as in xemu's default.

This is a work in progress. Rendering, audio, input, and gameplay can have
regressions; a successful build does not establish that every feature works.
System Link works between copies on one PC or a LAN; for copies on other
networks, set `RECOMP_NET_PEERS=<ip>:<port>` and open that UDP port. Xbox Live
names resolve to [Insignia](https://insignia.live)'s servers with no DNS setting,
but signing in needs an Insignia account on the virtual console and is not yet
verified. Make the account in xemu, copy it over with
`py scripts/import_xemu_accounts.py <xbox_hdd.qcow2> <save dir>`, and give the
game that console's keys in `RECOMP_XBOX_HDKEY`, `RECOMP_XBOX_SIGKEY` and
`RECOMP_XBOX_LANKEY` (32 hex digits each).

**Back up your saves before testing new builds.** This experimental software is
provided as is, without warranty. Use it at your own risk, including the risk
of crashes, corrupted saves, or lost progress.

## Development

- [Setup script](scripts/setup.ps1): toolchain checks, extraction, generation, and build.
- [Generator](scripts/generate_mm3.py): the pinned translation recipe; use it for regeneration.
- [Launcher source](src/mm3_launcher.cpp): settings and environment-variable mappings.
- [Runtime](tools/xboxrecomp): graphics, audio, input, networking, and runtime diagnostics.
- [Developer tools](tools/debug-features/README.md) and [teleport debugger](DEBUG_TELEPORT.md).
- [ImGui debug tools](IMGUI_DEBUG_TOOLS.md): optional in-game controls and current verification status.
- [Third-party licences](THIRD_PARTY.md).

PRs and cleanups are welcome, including fixes to AI-written code and incorrect
documentation. See [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to submit PRs, report
bugs, and describe local testing. AI-assisted contributions are welcome; review
and understand your changes before submitting them.

## Copyright and contributions

Midtown Madness 3 and Xbox software, assets, names, and trademarks belong to
their respective rights holders. This project grants no rights to that material.
Use your own lawfully obtained game dump and comply with applicable law;
owning a copy does not by itself grant permission to redistribute it.

Do not commit, upload, or attach any of the following to this repository,
issues, PRs, or releases:

- Disc images, game executables, DLC, or extracted game assets such as textures,
  models, music, movies, and archives.
- Original or leaked game source, or disassembled, decompiled, or generated
  translations of game code. Generate translated code locally during setup.
- Xbox BIOS/firmware, encryption keys, proprietary SDK files, or private saves
  and account data.
- Links to unauthorised copies of these materials.

Submit only code and materials you created or have permission to share, and
preserve applicable third-party notices. Report copyright concerns through an
issue without reposting the disputed material.

## Licence

Original project code is licensed under the [GNU General Public License,
version 3](LICENSE) (`GPL-3.0-only`). Original contributions submitted to this
project are provided under the same licence.

When distributing covered binaries or modified versions, comply with GPLv3,
including its corresponding-source and licensing requirements. Private
modifications do not have to be published. Earlier revisions released under
MIT remain available under MIT; this change does not revoke those permissions.

Third-party components retain their own licences; see [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md)
and the [runtime's licence](tools/xboxrecomp/LICENSE). Preserve their notices
and comply with their terms when combining or distributing code.

This licence covers only rights the project's contributors can grant. It does

metadata.description: The Darkness (2007, Starbreeze) toward VR on PC: our own Xbox 360 static recompilation runs in 3D, and the two-eye picture is being built. Non-commercial fan project; no game assets.

readme_text:
# The Darkness (2007) — working toward VR

Notes and tooling for getting **The Darkness** (Starbreeze, 2007) playable on PC and then into a
VR headset.

The Darkness never had a PC release — it shipped on Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 and stayed there.
A community **static recompilation** to native PC is in progress elsewhere. This repository is not that
port: we built our own, with the open ReXGlue toolkit and files from a disc we own, as the base for VR.

**This is the project we most want in VR.** Everything here is aimed at that.

## What is here

| Folder | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| [`engine-research/`](engine-research/) | [`ENGINE-DOSSIER.md`](engine-research/ENGINE-DOSSIER.md) — what is actually known about the game's files and engine, with confidence tags |
| [`dev-archive/`](dev-archive/) | Working source, scripts and reverse-engineering evidence |
| [`modding-notes/`](modding-notes/) | Dated field notes from each working session, including what did **not** work |

## Status

**Our own PC build plays in real-time 3D, and the two-eye picture is being built.**

Our build first reached live gameplay on 2026-09-16 and made its first left/right stereo pair on
2026-09-18. Since 2026-10-12 each picture knows which eye it is for, and both eyes can show the same
moment (seen in one test so far). Confirming that pair and taking it into the headset comes next.

Like the community ports, it ships no game content: every user supplies the files from their own copy.

## Why VR is realistic here, eventually

The route runs through the recompilation, not around it. A static recompilation turns the original
Xbox 360 code into **readable, buildable C++**, which means stereo rendering can be added *at the
source* rather than injected into a sealed binary from outside.

We have already done exactly that groundwork on a closely-related project —
[**condemned-2-vr**](https://github.com/TefMeister/condemned-2-vr), another 2007-08 Xbox 360 title
now running on PC from a self-built recompilation. The build knowledge, the fixes and the renderer
notes there apply directly here.

## What this is not

- **Not the PC port**, not a fork of it, and not affiliated with whoever is building it.
- **No game content.** No assets, executables or disc images — nothing from the game. You need your
  own legitimate copy.
- **Unfinished.** Nothing here is a supported product.

## Caution

Experimental and unfinished. Any VR build that comes out of this may cause **severe motion sickness
and discomfort**. That warning will only be removed for a build once it has been played through and
confirmed comfortable.

## Credits

- **Starbreeze Studios**, who made the game, and **2K Games**, who published it.
- **Whoever is building the PC recompilation** — the hard part is theirs. Credit will be named here
  properly once the project is public.
- **The [ReXGlue](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) project**, for the Xbox 360 recompilation
  toolkit this class of port is built on.
- **[Redump](http://redump.org/)**, whose drive and firmware documentation made reading the disc
  possible, and the **Kreon** firmware authors.
- **[redumper](https://github.com/superg/redumper)** (superg) and **[xdvdfs](https://github.com/antangelo/xdvdfs)**
  (antangelo), the tools used to copy the disc and read it.

If you should be credited here and are not, or want something changed or removed, please get in
touch and it will be put right as fast as we can.

## Legal

A non-commercial fan project. It requires you to own a legitimate copy of the game and redistributes
no original assets.

## Licence

**BSD 3-Clause** — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). Deliberately the same licence as the
[ReXGlue SDK](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) and the recompilation projects it supports, so
that fixes can move freely in either direction without a licensing conversation.

It covers the code and notes in this repository only. It grants **no rights in any game or asset** —
none are included here, and you need your own legitimate copy of the game.

readme_text:
# God of War — Tobiichi Port **English** · [Türkçe](README.tr.md) · [Español](README.es.md) **A native PC port of *God of War* (PlayStation 2, NTSC-U `SCUS-97399`) for Linux and Windows. The game's code is statically recompiled from MIPS to C++; the PS2 hardware is replaced by native code, not emulated.** ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Linux%20%7C%20Windows%20x64-0078D6) ![Language](https://img.shields.io/badge/C%2B%2B-20-00599C?logo=cplusplus&logoColor=white) ![Renderer](https://img.shields.io/badge/renderer-OpenGL-5586A4?logo=opengl&logoColor=white) ![Launcher](https://img.shields.io/badge/launcher-Qt%206-41CD52?logo=qt&logoColor=white) ![Based on](https://img.shields.io/badge/based%20on-PS2Recomp-8A2BE2) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--3.0-blue)
--- > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **contains no game files** (ISO, executable, IRX modules, `.PAK` data) and no code generated from > them. You need **your own legal copy** of *God of War* for the PS2 (USA version, `SCUS-97399`). The installer > builds everything on your computer from your own disc image; nothing derived from the game ever leaves it. ## Contents - [About the name](#about-the-name) - [What is this?](#what-is-this) - [Features](#features) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation on Windows](#installation-on-windows) - [Installation on Linux](#installation-on-linux) - [Playing](#playing) - [Performance](#performance) - [Updating](#updating) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Repository layout](#repository-layout) - [Contributors](#contributors) - [Credits and license](#credits-and-license) ## About the name The project is named after **Origami Tobiichi** (鳶一折紙), from the anime and light novel series ***Date A Live*** (DAL). ## What is this? Instead of emulating the PlayStation 2 one instruction at a time, this project **translates the game's original executable (`SCUS_973.99`) into C++** with [PS2Recomp](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) and compiles it into a native program. Around the game code sits a runtime that does the PS2 hardware's job natively: | PS2 part | In this port | |---|---| | **EE CPU** (game code) | Recompiled to C++ (~6,400 functions) | | **VU1** (vector unit microcode) | Compiled ahead of time to C++ from the microcode the game uses | | **GS** (graphics) | Native OpenGL renderer with GPU render targets, internal resolution 1×–4× | | **IOP** (I/O CPU) | The game's IRX modules compiled ahead of time to C++ | | **Sound, pad, memory card, movies** | Native services: sound engine, gamepad/keyboard/mouse, `.ps2` memory card, MPEG-2 movies (libmpeg2) | ## Features | | | |---|---| | **Launcher** | Graphics card, window/fullscreen, resolution, aspect ratio, image filter, internal resolution, frame-rate limit, keyboard layout, cheats — Turkish, English and Spanish | | **Widescreen** | Real Hor+ camera (16:9, 16:10, 21:9) based on the PCSX2 patch; movies switch to the game's own widescreen versions and fill the screen | | **Image** | Soft bilinear or bicubic with adjustable sharpening, optional FXAA | | **Movies** | Every movie plays natively at real speed, with its sound | | **Original look** | The game's own PlayStation button prompts and HUD | | **Keyboard and mouse** | A full, remappable keyboard and mouse layout; any gamepad works too | | **Lock-on** | **Alt** locks onto the nearest enemy; move the mouse left/right to switch targets | | **Agile combat** | Attacks and blocks come out of a roll sooner, and a missed attack press is retried for a moment | | **Cheat menu** | **F2** in game: god mode, one-hit kills, infinite magic and Rage of the Gods, max orbs, all upgrades and powers, unlock all extras | | **On-screen FPS** | Game and window frame rates in a corner (launcher option) | ## Requirements - **Your own *God of War* (USA, `SCUS-97399`) disc image** as an `.iso` file (about 8 GB). Make it from your own disc with any DVD ripping tool. - **20 GB of free disk space** (the extracted disc, about 8 GB, plus the build). - **A 64-bit x86 CPU** (4 cores or more recommended; on Windows it must support **AVX2**, which every Intel CPU since 2013 and every AMD CPU since 2015 does) and **8 GB of RAM** (16 GB recommended while building). - **A GPU with OpenGL 4.3 or newer**: any NVIDIA/AMD card, or the integrated graphics of a recent Intel/AMD CPU. - **Windows 10/11 x64** or a **Linux** distribution (Arch/CachyOS, Ubuntu 24.04+, Fedora 40+ or similar). - Time: the first build takes **30–90 minutes** depending on the CPU. Later updates only rebuild what changed. ## Installation on Windows 1. **Get the project.** Click **Code → Download ZIP** on GitHub and unzip it, or with Git: ```bat git clone https://github.com/YYOzcan/Tobiichi-Port.git ``` Use a short path without special characters if you can (for example `C:\Games\Tobiichi-Port`). 2. **Copy your disc image** into the `game` folder of the project and name it `God of War.iso`. 3. **First time only — install the build tools.** Open the project folder, type `cmd` in the address bar, press Enter and run: ```bat instalar.cmd -Herramientas ``` This installs Git, Python 3 and the Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (C++ compiler, CMake and Ninja) with `winget`. Windows asks for administrator permission; accept it. It takes 15–30 minutes and then continues with step 4 on its own. 4. **Build.** If the tools are already installed, simply **double-click `instalar.cmd`**. The installer: 1. extracts the disc into `game\` (the `.iso` is no longer needed afterwards); 2. builds the recompiler and translates `SCUS_973.99` into C++; 3. builds the game (`ps2EntryRunner.exe`) and the launcher — Qt 6 is downloaded automatically into `herramientas\qt` if it is not installed; 4. **optimizes**: the game opens by itself for 4 minutes and plays the start of the first level with automatic button presses. **Do not touch the keyboard or mouse during this step.** It records the VU1 microcode and the IOP modules the game uses and rebuilds them as native code (much faster); 5. creates a **God Of War - Tobiichi Port** shortcut on the desktop and in the Start menu. 5. **Play** from the shortcut. In the launcher, check the **Files** tab once (everything should be detected) and press **PLAY**. Options: `instalar.cmd -Iso "D:\path\God of War.iso"` uses an image from another folder; `-SinOptimizar` skips step 4.4; `-Optimizar` repeats it later. ## Installation on Linux 1. **Install the dependencies.** - **Arch / CachyOS / Manjaro:** ```bash sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel cmake ninja python git qt6-base qt6-declarative qt6-svg ``` - **Ubuntu / Debian:** ```bash sudo apt install build-essential cmake ninja-build python3 git libgl-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev \ libxinerama-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libasound2-dev qt6-base-dev qt6-declarative-dev \ qml6-module-qtquick-controls qml6-module-qtquick-layouts qml6-module-qtquick-dialogs \ qml6-module-qtquick-effects qml6-module-qtquick-shapes qml6-module-qtquick-particles qml6-module-qtcore ``` - **Fedora:** ```bash sudo dnf install gcc-c++ cmake ninja-build python3 git mesa-libGL-devel libX11-devel libXrandr-devel \ libXinerama-devel libXcursor-devel libXi-devel libxkbcommon-devel wayland-devel alsa-lib-devel \ qt6-qtbase-devel qt6-qtdeclarative-devel ``` 2. **Get the project:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/YYOzcan/Tobiichi-Port.git cd Tobiichi-Port ``` 3. **Copy your disc image** to `game/God of War.iso` (or pass its path in the next step). 4. **Run the installer:** ```bash ./instalar.sh # or: ./instalar.sh "/path/to/God of War.iso" ``` It does the same steps as on Windows: extracts the disc into `game/`, generates the C++ code, builds the game and the launcher, **optimizes** (the game opens by itself for 4 minutes — do not touch the keyboard or mouse) and adds **God Of War: Tobiichi Port** to the applications menu. Options: `--sin-optimizar`, `--optimizar [seconds]`, `--jobs N`. 5. **Play** from the applications menu, or `launcher/build/tobiichi-launcher`. Without the launcher: `./run_gow.sh`. ## Playing **Keyboard and mouse (default layout, remappable in the launcher):** | Action | Key | Action | Key | |---|---|---|---| | Move | **W A S D** | Evade (right stick) | **Ctrl + W A S D** | | Light attack (□) | **Left click** | Heavy attack (△) | **Right click** | | Jump (✕) | **Space** | Grab (○) | **F** | | Block (L1) | **Q** | R1 | **E** | | L2 / R2 (magic) | **Shift / Ctrl** | Rage of the Gods | **V** | | Magic 1–4 | **1 2 3 4** | Blade of Artemis (L1 + R1) | **Middle click** | | D-pad | **Arrow keys** | Camera (right stick) | **I J K L** | | Start / Select | **Enter / Tab** | Lock-on | **Alt** (mouse switches target) | **Hotkeys:** **F2** cheat menu · **F11** fullscreen · **F1** developer panel. **Gamepads:** DualShock 4, DualSense, Xbox and other controllers work out of the box (vibration on Windows). **Memory card:** saves go to `game/Mcd001.ps2` (a PCSX2-compatible card image; you can copy your PCSX2 card there). ## Performance The game's logic is tied to the PS2's 60 Hz VBlank, so **the game itself never runs above 60 FPS**; the port keeps it at real speed (it drops frames rather than slowing down). - **Dedicated GPU (NVIDIA/AMD):** internal resolution 2×–3× at 60 FPS is typical. - **Integrated graphics** (for example Radeon 680M): 1×–2×. Measured on the ship deck combat at 1×: 50–60 FPS with the *performance* power profile; on battery/*power saver* the CPU clock drops and so does the frame rate. - The heaviest part is the VU1 thread (CPU). Running the optimization step again after playing new areas (`./instalar.sh --optimizar` / `instalar.cmd -Optimizar`) turns more of it into native code. ## Updating ```bash git pull ./instalar.sh # Windows: instalar.cmd ``` Only the files that changed are rebuilt; the extracted disc and the recorded VU1/IOP code are kept. ## Troubleshooting | Problem | Fix | |---|---| | "I can't find the ISO" | Put it at `game/God of War.iso` or pass the path to the installer. Only the USA version (`SCUS-97399`) works. | | The game runs slowly | Run the optimization step (`--optimizar`); choose 1× or 2× internal resolution; use the *performance* power profile on laptops. | | The launcher did not build on Linux | Install the Qt 6 packages listed above, then run `./instalar.sh` again. `./run_gow.sh` plays without it. | | Windows: "Visual Studio is missing" | Run `instalar.cmd -Herramientas`. | | Black screen or crash on an old GPU | The renderer needs OpenGL 4.3; update the graphics driver. | | Where are the logs? | Launcher: **Other → Last game log**. Installer: `build-gen/` (`recomp.log`, `optimizar.log`). | ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR ISO[Your God of War ISO] --> X[instalar: extract to game/] X --> ELF[SCUS_973.99] ELF --> R[ps2_recomp] M[config/funcmap.csv
recomp.template.toml] --> R R --> C[~6,400 C++ files] O[src/gow_overrides.cpp] --> B[CMake + Ninja] C --> B RT[PS2Recomp runtime
GS, VU1, IOP, sound] --> B V[VU1 and IOP code
recorded by instalar] --> B B --> G[ps2EntryRunner] L[Launcher] -->|settings| G ``` More: [`docs/ULTIMATE.md`](docs/ULTIMATE.md) (this release, in Spanish), [`docs/waffle/`](docs/waffle/README.md) (Waffle565's documentation of the runtime, in English), [`docs/`](docs/) (research log and older notes, in Spanish). ## Repository layout ``` . ├── instalar.sh / instalar.cmd / instalar.ps1 # installers (Linux / Windows) ├── run_gow.sh # play without the launcher (Linux) ├── game/ # your extracted disc goes here (ignored by git) ├── config/ # function map and recompiler configuration (incl. widescreen patch) ├── src/ # game overrides (gow_overrides.cpp) ├── PS2Recomp/ # recompiler and runtime (GS, VU1, IOP, sound, pad, memory card) ├── launcher/ # God Of War: Tobiichi Launcher (Qt 6) ├── tools/ # VU1/IOP code generators, ISO extractor, diagnostics └── docs/ # documentation ``` ## Contributors

YYOzcan
Tobiichi Port: Linux port, launcher, widescreen, gameplay extras, integration
Waffle565
God-Of-War-Native-Port: native GS renderer, IOP and VU1 compiled to C++, movies, sound, memory card
KIexster
god-of-war-recomp: the God of War recompilation pipeline, VU1 compiler and runtime fixes this port is built on
## Credits and license - [**PS2Recomp**](https://github.com/ran-j/PS2Recomp) by ran-j and contributors — recompiler and runtime (GPL-3.0). - [**LightVelox's SotC runtime fork**](https://github.com/LightVelox/PS2Recomp/tree/ac9efa070638ad3b3accd284de6f898d5ab271d1) (Taylor N. Albarnaz) — OpenGL GS context and EE fixes (GPL-3.0). - [**PCSX2**](https://github.com/PCSX2/pcsx2) — reference for verification; VU interpreter and EE reference code (GPL-3.0+). - Widescreen based on the PCSX2 "Widescreen 16:9" patch for SCUS-97399 by nemesis2000 and CRASHARKI. - [libmpeg2](https://libmpeg2.sourceforge.io/) (GPL-2.0+), [raylib](https://www.raylib.com/) (zlib), [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui) (MIT), [Qt 6](https://www.qt.io/) (LGPL-3.0), [Cinzel](https://github.com/NDISCOVER/Cinzel) font (SIL OFL 1.1). - *God of War* © Sony Interactive Entertainment / Santa Monica Studio. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony. No game content is distributed. *Date A Live* and Origami Tobiichi © Koushi Tachibana / Tsunako / KADOKAWA. The code in this repository is released under the **GNU General Public License v3.0**, like PS2Recomp. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

readme_text:
# CryRecomp

Experimental **native static recompilation** research project targeting *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (Nintendo Switch). **Not a playable port.**

## Live progress

The project has a live GitHub Pages dashboard that derives its state from the integration checkpoint log, open PRs and the active lifter branch:

**https://xzhuofan.github.io/CryRecomp/**

Source of truth for integration milestones: [coordination PR #4](https://github.com/xzhuofan/CryRecomp/pull/4).

## Current status

Development has moved beyond bootstrap: the retail module set has been parsed and linked, the complete measured relocation batch has been applied, and recompiled game code has reached `nnMain`. Fixed-base code generation, tail-PLT boundaries and Horizon IPC bring-up are active work. Use the live dashboard above for the current checkpoint rather than treating this README paragraph as a real-time status report.

## Build and test

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --parallel
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/cryrecomp inspect /path/to/your/main.nso
```

On Windows, use the executable produced in `build/Release/cryrecomp.exe` for multi-config generators.

## Design priorities

1. Deterministic binary identity and validation, with support tracked per build ID.
2. Ahead-of-time AArch64 recompilation to native code (planned).
3. Explicit Horizon/SDK boundary and application runtime (planned).
4. NVN/Vulkan rendering backend (planned; Metal can be evaluated later).
5. Differential regression tests, functional parity, performance profiling.

No Nintendo code, game assets, console keys, copyrighted game data, or download URLs are distributed or checked in. Users provide legally obtained local input. Do not commit secrets. Inspect downloaded binaries in isolation before running generated code.

## Technical references

- https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp
- https://github.com/Denkishi/ssbu-recomp

References are not vendored and no third-party source has been copied. Review individual licenses before incorporating code.

See [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md).
